entries.name: when
entries.desc: Evaluate body ... in order when test is true (anything but #f).
entries.returns: The value of the last body expression; void when test is #f.

entries.name: unless
entries.desc: Evaluate body ... in order when test is #f.
entries.returns: The value of the last body expression; void when test is true.

entries.name: and
entries.desc: Evaluate tests left to right, stopping at the first #f.
entries.returns: #f at the first false test (the rest is not evaluated), else the value of the last test; #t with no tests.

entries.name: or
entries.desc: Evaluate tests left to right, stopping at the first true value.
entries.returns: The first value that is not #f (the rest is not evaluated); #f when every test is #f or there are none.

entries.name: cond
entries.desc: Evaluate the clause of the first true test; (test => proc) calls proc on the test value.
entries.returns: The value of the last expression of the selected clause; the test value for a clause without expressions; proc's result for =>. Void when no clause matches and there is no else.
entries.example:
(define (sign n) (cond ((< n 0) 'negative) ((= n 0) 'zero) (else 'positive)))
(sign -4)                            ; => negative
(cond ((assv 2 '((1 . one) (2 . two))) => cdr) (else 'none))  ; => two
(void? (cond (#f 1)))                ; => #t

entries.name: if
entries.desc: Evaluate then when test is true (anything but #f, even 0 and ()), else the else branch.
entries.returns: The value of the branch taken; void when test is #f and else is omitted.

entries.name: lambda
entries.desc: Create a procedure. params is (a b ...), (a b . rest) or one symbol bound to the list of all arguments.
entries.returns: A procedure (a closure over the variables in scope).
entries.example:
(define add (lambda (a b) (+ a b)))
(add 2 3)                            ; => 5
((lambda (first . rest) rest) 1 2 3) ; => (2 3)
((lambda args (length args)) 'a 'b)  ; => 2
entries.notes: Calls are not arity-checked: a missing argument reads as void and extra arguments are ignored.

entries.name: let
entries.desc: Bind local variables in parallel and evaluate body; the named form binds name to a loop procedure.
entries.returns: The value of the last body expression.
entries.example:
(let ((x 2) (y 3)) (* x y))          ; => 6
(let loop ((i 0) (acc '()))
  (if (= i 3) (reverse acc) (loop (+ i 1) (cons i acc))))  ; => (0 1 2)

entries.name: let*
entries.desc: Bind local variables sequentially (each init sees the previous ones) and evaluate body.
entries.returns: The value of the last body expression.

entries.name: define
entries.desc: Bind a global (at top level) or a local (at the start of a body); the second form defines a procedure.
entries.returns: At top level the name as a symbol (a redefinition replaces the value); an internal define returns void.
entries.example:
(define limit 10)                    ; => limit
(define (square n) (* n n))
(square 7)                           ; => 49
(define (hyp2 a b) (define s (+ (square a) (square b))) s)
(hyp2 3 4)                           ; => 25

entries.name: set!
entries.desc: Assign a new value to an existing local or global variable.
entries.returns: Void. An error "set!: unbound variable" when var is neither a local nor a defined global.
entries.example:
(define count 0)
(set! count (+ count 1))
count                                ; => 1
(set! no-such-var 5)                 ; => error: unbound variable

entries.name: begin
entries.desc: Evaluate expressions in order; at top level its definitions stay global.
entries.returns: The value of the last expression; void for (begin).
entries.example:
(define total 0)
(begin (set! total (+ total 5)) (set! total (* total 2)) total)  ; => 10
(void? (begin))                      ; => #t

entries.name: quote
entries.desc: Return datum without evaluating it.
entries.returns: datum itself: a symbol, list, vector or constant. Quoted data is a constant: do not mutate it (it may live in the read-only Code ROM).

entries.name: define-syntax
entries.desc: Define a syntax-rules macro, expanded at compile time; locals introduced by the template are renamed.
entries.returns: The macro name as a symbol. A use that matches no rule is a compile error "no syntax-rules pattern matched".
entries.example:
(define-syntax swap!
  (syntax-rules () ((_ a b) (let ((tmp a)) (set! a b) (set! b tmp)))))
(define x 1)
(define y 2)
(swap! x y)
(list x y)                           ; => (2 1)
entries.notes: Template symbols that are pattern variables, literals, special forms or defined globals are kept as written; other symbols the template introduces get fresh names.

entries.name: syntax-rules
entries.desc: The rules of define-syntax: the first pattern matching the form selects its template; x ... repeats.
entries.returns: A macro transformer; valid only as the second operand of define-syntax (elsewhere it is an unbound variable).
entries.example:
(define-syntax my-or
  (syntax-rules ()
    ((_) #f)
    ((_ e) e)
    ((_ e r ...) (let ((t e)) (if t t (my-or r ...))))))
(my-or #f #f 3)                      ; => 3
entries.notes: The keyword position of a pattern is ignored (write _). Literals match only the same symbol.

entries.name: define-macro
entries.desc: Define a non-hygienic macro: body builds the expansion from the unevaluated operands, at compile time.
entries.returns: The macro name as a symbol.
entries.example:
(define-macro (inc! var . by)
  (list 'set! var (list '+ var (if (null? by) 1 (car by)))))
(define n 5)
(inc! n)
(inc! n 10)
n                                    ; => 16

entries.name: void
entries.desc: Return the void value, the result of forms with nothing to return.
entries.returns: Void (what (if #f #f) returns); arguments are ignored. write prints void as nothing.

entries.name: include-bytes
entries.desc: The file's bytes as a string. Compiled code gets them at compile time (embedded in the image), e.g. fonts.
entries.returns: A string of the file's bytes (NUL bytes included). A missing file is a compile error "include-bytes: cannot read file".
entries.example:
(define digits (include-bytes "fonts/digits-48.mfnt"))
(font-register! 3 digits)            ; => #t
(include-bytes "no-such-file.bin")   ; => error: include-bytes: cannot read file
entries.notes: The path is relative to the working directory of the compiler (tools/build_apps.py: the repository root). The example needs a font file the test VM lacks.

entries.name: exit
entries.desc: Terminate the Scheme process with status code (default 0).
entries.returns: Does not return. A code that is not an integer exits with status 0.
entries.notes: Ends the host process (PC REPL). The board has no process to end: the C exit() of the firmware stops it, and the WASM simulator's exit() spins forever. Apps should return to the launcher instead.

entries.name: error
entries.desc: Raise an error with message msg, aborting the current evaluation.
entries.returns: Does not return. The error message is msg when it is a string, else "error"; the further arguments are ignored.
entries.example:
(define (safe-div a b)
  (if (= b 0) (error "safe-div: division by zero") (/ a b)))
(safe-div 10 2)                      ; => 5
(safe-div 1 0)                       ; => error: division by zero

entries.name: call/cc
entries.desc: Call proc with the current continuation k; calling (k v) returns v from call/cc.
entries.returns: What proc returns, or the value passed to the continuation. Continuations are re-entrant. An error when proc is not a procedure or not exactly 1 argument is given, and when k is called from inside a C primitive (for-each, map, ...).
entries.example:
(+ 1 (call/cc (lambda (k) (k 10) 20)))      ; => 11
(define (first-neg lst)
  (call/cc (lambda (return)
    (let loop ((l lst)) (cond ((null? l) #f) ((< (car l) 0) (return (car l))) (else (loop (cdr l))))))))
(first-neg '(3 -2 5))                       ; => -2
(call/cc (lambda (k) (for-each k '(1 2))))  ; => error: foreign C frame
entries.notes: A continuation cannot be invoked across a C primitive that called back into Scheme (for-each, map, apply of a callback, ...): "cannot invoke continuation across foreign C frame boundary". Escape from a Scheme loop instead.

entries.name: call-with-current-continuation
entries.desc: Full name of call/cc.
entries.returns: As call/cc: what proc returns, or the value passed to the continuation.

entries.name: apply
entries.desc: Call proc with arg1 ... followed by the elements of the list rest.
entries.returns: What proc returns. An error with fewer than 2 arguments, when rest is not a proper list, or when proc is not callable.

entries.name: number?
entries.desc: Test if obj is a number (fixnum, bignum or flonum).
entries.returns: #t or #f.

entries.name: integer?
entries.desc: Test if obj is an exact integer (fixnum or bignum); integral flonums such as 7.0 are not.
entries.returns: #t or #f.

entries.name: real?
entries.desc: Test if obj is a real number; the same as number? (there are no complex numbers).
entries.returns: #t or #f.

entries.name: flonum?
entries.desc: Test if obj is an inexact flonum.
entries.returns: #t or #f.

entries.name: symbol?
entries.desc: Test if obj is a symbol.
entries.returns: #t or #f.

entries.name: procedure?
entries.desc: Test if obj is a procedure: a closure, a primitive or a continuation.
entries.returns: #t or #f.

entries.name: char?
entries.desc: Test if obj is a character. Characters are fixnum code points (#\a is 97), so any fixnum passes.
entries.returns: #t for any fixnum, else #f.

entries.name: boolean?
entries.desc: Test if obj is a boolean (#t or #f).
entries.returns: #t or #f.

entries.name: eq?
entries.desc: Identity: the same object; fixnums, characters, symbols, booleans and () compare by value.
entries.returns: #t or #f (#f also for a wrong argument count).
entries.notes: Equal literal constants of one compiled unit may be shared, so (eq? "ab" "ab") can be #t.

entries.name: equal?
entries.desc: Structural equality: pairs, vectors and strings element by element, numbers by type and value.
entries.returns: #t or #f (1 and 1.0 are not equal?).

entries.name: not
entries.desc: #t when obj is #f, else #f (only #f is false; () and 0 are true).
entries.returns: #t or #f.

entries.name: void?
entries.desc: Test if obj is the void value.
entries.returns: #t or #f.

entries.name: eqv?
entries.desc: eq? that also compares numbers by value; an exact and an inexact number are never eqv? (0 and 0.0).
entries.returns: #t or #f.

entries.name: list?
entries.desc: Test if obj is a proper list (ending in ()).
entries.returns: #t or #f.
entries.notes: Does not detect cycles: a circular list never returns.

entries.name: display
entries.desc: Print obj to the console in human-readable form (strings without quotes).
entries.returns: Void.
entries.example:
(display "Temp: ")                   ; prints Temp:
(display 21.5)                       ; prints 21.5
(display '(1 "two" c))               ; prints (1 two c)
(newline)
entries.notes: Characters are code points and print as numbers (#\a prints 97); void prints nothing.

entries.name: write
entries.desc: Print obj to the console in read-back syntax (strings in quotes).
entries.returns: Void.
entries.notes: Strings print in double quotes with \" \\ \n \t \r escaped (other control bytes as \xHH;); characters print as numbers; void prints nothing.

entries.name: newline
entries.desc: Print a newline character to the console.
entries.returns: Void.

entries.name: print
entries.desc: Print arguments separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
entries.returns: Void.
entries.example:
(print "x =" 42)                     ; prints x = 42
(print)                              ; prints an empty line

entries.name: load
entries.desc: Read, compile and evaluate every expression of a Scheme source file. Not for apps: only the system settings and the REPL may (an app gets an error).
entries.returns: The value of the last expression of the file. An error when the file cannot be opened, or when the VM has no compiler (the firmware VM: "compiler not available").
entries.notes: Needs the Scheme compiler in the VM (PC REPL); the firmware runs precompiled code.

entries.name: dump-fasl
entries.desc: Serialize the VM heap to a FASL file; the default portable 32-bit layout loads on every target, 'native is for load-fasl-xip.
entries.returns: #t. An error when the file cannot be created or written, or the layout is not 'portable or 'native.
entries.notes: The example writes files into the working directory. A failed dump removes the partial file.

entries.name: load-fasl
entries.desc: Replace the VM heap (globals included) with a FASL image written by dump-fasl.
entries.returns: #t. An error when the file cannot be opened or is not a FASL image ("invalid FASL magic header").
entries.notes: The code that called load-fasl does not continue: its top-level form returns #t at once, so call it last in a form. The example needs the file of dump-fasl.

entries.name: load-fasl-xip
entries.desc: Load a FASL image for execute-in-place: its objects stay in the read-only image instead of being copied to the heap.
entries.returns: #t; (xip-active?) is #t afterwards. An error when the file cannot be opened or is not a FASL image.
entries.notes: Write the image with (dump-fasl path 'native). As with load-fasl, the calling top-level form returns #t at once. The example needs the file of dump-fasl.

entries.name: eof-object
entries.desc: The end-of-file object.
entries.returns: The unique end-of-file object, written #<eof>.

entries.name: eof-object?
entries.desc: True for the end-of-file object.
entries.returns: #t or #f.

entries.name: help
entries.desc: Print the syntax, category and description of name (a symbol or string); (help) lists every entry.
entries.returns: Void (the text goes to the console). An error when name is not a symbol or string, or with more than one argument.
entries.notes: An unknown name prints "No documentation found". A firmware built with MINISCHEME_NO_HELP prints that help is disabled.

entries.name: global-names
entries.desc: Every global name, including primitives not used yet.
entries.returns: A list of symbols in no particular order, internal %-prefixed names included.

entries.name: user-globals
entries.desc: Globals defined after the baseline environment.
entries.returns: A list of symbols, oldest definition first; () when nothing was defined.

entries.name: defined?
entries.desc: True when name has a global binding or primitive.
entries.returns: #t or #f (#f for special forms such as if, and for reserved or device-only names the VM lacks). An error when the argument is not a symbol.

entries.name: xip-active?
entries.desc: True when a FASL image runs in place (load-fasl-xip); an app in the Code ROM shows in vm-rom-bytes instead.
entries.returns: #t or #f.

entries.name: xip-stats
entries.desc: The XIP image: an alist of its base address, size in bytes and count of C function references.
entries.returns: () when no XIP image is loaded, else ((cfuncs . n) (rom-size . bytes) (rom-base . address)).

entries.name: vm-allocated-bytes
entries.desc: Bytes in use in the VM heap (nursery and tenured space, garbage not collected yet included).
entries.returns: A non-negative integer.

entries.name: vm-heap-size
entries.desc: VM heap capacity in bytes (the tenured space; the nursery is extra).
entries.returns: A positive integer.

entries.name: vm-stack-depth
entries.desc: Value stack slots in use.
entries.returns: A non-negative integer.

entries.name: vm-frame-depth
entries.desc: Call frames in use.
entries.returns: A positive integer.
entries.notes: Tail calls reuse the frame, so (define (f) (g)) does not add one.

entries.name: vm-rom-bytes
entries.desc: Size of the attached Code ROM image (0 when the app runs from RAM).
entries.returns: A non-negative integer.

entries.name: vm-stats
entries.desc: VM counters: GCs, allocation, live and peak heap, stack and frame peaks.
entries.returns: An alist of integers: alloc-kb (allocated since start), minor-gcs, major-gcs, live-bytes and live-peak (tenured bytes after the last / largest GC), stack-peak, frame-peak, stack-slots, frame-slots (capacities), rom-bytes.
entries.example:
(map car (vm-stats))
; => (alloc-kb minor-gcs major-gcs live-bytes live-peak stack-peak frame-peak stack-slots frame-slots rom-bytes)
(integer? (cdr (assq 'minor-gcs (vm-stats))))  ; => #t

entries.name: vm-stack-trace
entries.desc: Query or enable/disable stack trace capture upon errors (enabled by default in WASM, disabled on hardware).
entries.returns: A boolean indicating whether stack trace capture is enabled.

entries.desc: Return the sum of the arguments (0 if no arguments).
entries.returns: The sum: an exact integer (a bignum when it overflows the fixnum range), or a flonum when any argument is a flonum; an error when an argument is not a number.
entries.notes: Numbers are exact integers (fixnums, promoted to bignums automatically when a result leaves the fixnum range: 29 bits on the 32-bit device and WASM, 61 bits on a 64-bit PC) or inexact flonums (C doubles). There are no rationals or complex numbers. A flonum argument makes the result a flonum. `write` prints a flonum with up to 15 significant digits and a trailing `.0` when it is integral (`3.5`, `2.0`, `0.333333333333333`).

entries.desc: Subtract following arguments from z1, or negate z1.
entries.returns: The difference, or the negation of z1 alone: exact integer or flonum as for `+`; an error with no argument or when an argument is not a number.

entries.desc: Return the product of the arguments (1 if no arguments).
entries.returns: The product: an exact integer (a bignum when it overflows), or a flonum when any argument is a flonum; an error when an argument is not a number.

entries.desc: Divide z1 by the following arguments, or return 1/z1. An inexact quotient of integers is a flonum (no rationals).
entries.returns: An exact integer when every division is exact, otherwise a flonum; an error "division by zero" when a divisor is 0 or 0.0, or when an argument is not a number.

entries.desc: Test if numbers are strictly monotonically increasing.
entries.returns: #t or #f; exact and inexact numbers compare by value. With fewer than two arguments #t. An error when a compared argument is not a number (comparison stops at the first #f).

entries.desc: Test if numbers are strictly monotonically decreasing.
entries.returns: #t or #f, as for `<`; an error when a compared argument is not a number.

entries.desc: Test if numbers are monotonically non-decreasing.
entries.returns: #t or #f, as for `<`; an error when a compared argument is not a number.

entries.desc: Test if numbers are monotonically non-increasing.
entries.returns: #t or #f, as for `<`; an error when a compared argument is not a number.

entries.desc: Test if all numbers are numerically equal.
entries.returns: #t or #f; an exact and an inexact number are equal when their values are (`(= 1 1.0)` is #t). An error when a compared argument is not a number.

entries.name: modulo
entries.desc: Return n1 modulo n2: the remainder with the sign of n2.
entries.returns: An exact integer with the sign of n2 (floor division); an error when an argument is not an exact integer (flonums are refused) or n2 is 0.

entries.name: remainder
entries.desc: Return the remainder of dividing n1 by n2, with the sign of n1.
entries.returns: An exact integer with the sign of n1 (truncating division); an error when an argument is not an exact integer or n2 is 0.

entries.name: quotient
entries.desc: Return the integer quotient of dividing n1 by n2, truncated towards zero.
entries.returns: An exact integer (bignums allowed); an error when an argument is not an exact integer (`(quotient 7.0 2)` fails) or n2 is 0.

entries.name: abs
entries.desc: Return the absolute value of x.
entries.returns: A number of the same exactness as x; an error when x is not a number.

entries.name: sqrt
entries.desc: Return the square root of z as a flonum.
entries.returns: A flonum, also for exact arguments (`(sqrt 16)` is 4.0); an error when z is negative or not a number.

entries.name: sin
entries.desc: Return the sine of z (in radians).
entries.returns: A flonum; an error when z is not a number.

entries.name: cos
entries.desc: Return the cosine of z (in radians).
entries.returns: A flonum; an error when z is not a number.

entries.name: tan
entries.desc: Return the tangent of z (in radians).
entries.returns: A flonum; an error when z is not a number.

entries.name: asin
entries.desc: Return the arcsine of z, in radians.
entries.returns: A flonum in [-pi/2, pi/2]; NaN when z is outside [-1, 1]; an error when z is not a number.

entries.name: acos
entries.desc: Return the arccosine of z, in radians.
entries.returns: A flonum in [0, pi]; NaN when z is outside [-1, 1]; an error when z is not a number.

entries.name: atan
entries.desc: Return the arctangent of y, or with x the angle of the point (x, y) (atan2).
entries.returns: A flonum in radians: in [-pi/2, pi/2] for one argument, in [-pi, pi] for two; an error when an argument is not a number.

entries.name: exp
entries.desc: Return e raised to the power of z.
entries.returns: A flonum; an error when z is not a number.

entries.name: log
entries.desc: Return the natural logarithm of z.
entries.returns: A flonum; an error when z is not positive or not a number. There is no two-argument form: divide by `(log base)`.

entries.name: expt
entries.desc: Return z1 raised to the power of z2.
entries.returns: An exact integer (bignum when large) for an exact base and a non-negative exact exponent; otherwise a flonum (also for a negative exact exponent); an error when an argument is not a number.

entries.name: floor
entries.desc: Return the largest integer <= x.
entries.returns: x itself for an exact integer, an integral flonum for a flonum (use `inexact->exact` for an exact result); an error when x is not a number.

entries.name: ceiling
entries.desc: Return the smallest integer >= x.
entries.returns: x itself for an exact integer, an integral flonum for a flonum; an error when x is not a number.

entries.name: round
entries.desc: Round x to the nearest integer; halves round away from zero (2.5 -> 3.0).
entries.returns: x itself for an exact integer, an integral flonum for a flonum; an error when x is not a number.
entries.notes: Unlike R7RS (round half to even), halves round away from zero (C `round`).

entries.name: truncate
entries.desc: Truncate x towards zero.
entries.returns: x itself for an exact integer, an integral flonum for a flonum; an error when x is not a number.

entries.name: exact?
entries.desc: Test if z is an exact number (fixnum or bignum).
entries.returns: #t for an exact integer, #f for a flonum; #f (no error) for a non-number.

entries.name: inexact?
entries.desc: Test if z is an inexact number (flonum).
entries.returns: #t for a flonum, #f for an exact integer; #f (no error) for a non-number.

entries.name: exact->inexact
entries.desc: Convert an exact number to an inexact flonum.
entries.returns: A flonum (a flonum argument is returned as a flonum of the same value; large bignums lose precision); an error when z is not a number.

entries.name: inexact->exact
entries.desc: Convert z to an exact integer, rounding a flonum to the nearest integer (halves away from zero).
entries.returns: An exact integer: z itself when exact, otherwise the flonum rounded to the nearest integer (no rationals), a bignum when large; an error when z is not a number, or is a NaN or infinity.

entries.name: max
entries.desc: The largest argument.
entries.returns: The largest argument itself, unconverted: `(max 3 2.0)` is the exact 3 (no inexact contagion, unlike R7RS); an error with no argument or a non-number.

entries.name: min
entries.desc: The smallest argument.
entries.returns: The smallest argument itself, unconverted (no inexact contagion); an error with no argument or a non-number.

entries.name: cons
entries.desc: Construct a new pair with car obj1 and cdr obj2.
entries.returns: A newly allocated pair; an error unless exactly 2 arguments are given.

entries.name: car
entries.desc: Return the first element of pair.
entries.returns: The car of pair; an error when pair is not a pair (including the empty list).
entries.example:
(car '(1 2 3))       ; => 1
(car '((a . b) c))   ; => (a . b)
(car '())            ; => error: requires a pair

entries.name: cdr
entries.desc: Return the second element of pair.
entries.returns: The cdr of pair (the rest of a list); an error when pair is not a pair.

entries.name: set-car!
entries.desc: Mutate the car field of pair.
entries.returns: Void; an error when pair is not a pair or is a quoted literal in the read-only code image.
entries.notes: Quoted literals of an app loaded from the read-only code image (XIP) cannot be modified: mutating one raises "cannot modify a literal constant". Mutate freshly allocated data (list, vector, cons, make-vector) instead.

entries.name: set-cdr!
entries.desc: Mutate the cdr field of pair.
entries.returns: Void; an error when pair is not a pair or is a quoted literal in the read-only code image.
entries.notes: Quoted literals of an app loaded from the read-only code image (XIP) cannot be modified: mutating one raises "cannot modify a literal constant". Mutate freshly allocated data (list, vector, cons, make-vector) instead.

entries.name: pair?
entries.desc: Return #t if obj is a pair, #f otherwise.
entries.returns: #t or #f; the empty list is not a pair.

entries.name: null?
entries.desc: Return #t if obj is empty list (), #f otherwise.
entries.returns: #t only for the empty list; #f for anything else (also #f and "").

entries.name: list
entries.desc: Return a newly allocated list of its arguments.
entries.returns: A new proper list; `()` with no arguments.

entries.name: length
entries.desc: Return the number of elements in list.
entries.returns: An exact integer; an error "not a proper list" for an improper list or a non-list.

entries.name: reverse
entries.desc: Return a newly allocated list with elements in reverse order.
entries.returns: A new list; the argument is not changed. Not checked: the tail of an improper list is dropped and a non-list gives `()`.

entries.name: append
entries.desc: Concatenate lists into a single list.
entries.returns: A list whose elements are copied from all arguments but the last, which is shared (it may be any object, giving an improper list); `()` with no arguments. Not checked: a non-list argument before the last counts as empty.

entries.name: map
entries.desc: Apply proc element-wise across lists and return list of results.
entries.returns: A new list of the results, in order; with several lists it stops at the end of the shortest. An error with no list or more than 4 lists, when proc is not a procedure, or when proc raises one.

entries.name: filter
entries.desc: Return a list of elements satisfying predicate pred.
entries.returns: A new list of the elements for which pred returns a true value, in their original order; an error unless 2 arguments are given or when pred raises one.

entries.name: fold-left
entries.desc: Left-associative fold: (proc ... (proc init x1) x2).
entries.returns: The last value of proc, called as (proc acc x) for each element from the left; init for an empty list. Exactly one list: an error otherwise.

entries.name: fold-right
entries.desc: Right-associative fold: (proc x1 (proc x2 ... init)).
entries.returns: The last value of proc, called as (proc x acc) for each element from the right; init for an empty list. Exactly one list: an error otherwise.

entries.name: caar
entries.desc: Equivalent to (car (car x)).
entries.returns: The car of the car of x; an error when x or its car is not a pair.
entries.example:
(caar '((1 2) 3))    ; => 1
(caar '(1))          ; => error: requires a pair in car

entries.name: cadr
entries.desc: Equivalent to (car (cdr x)): the second element.
entries.returns: The second element of x; an error when x or its cdr is not a pair.
entries.example:
(cadr '(1 2 3))      ; => 2
(cadr '(1))          ; => error: requires a pair in cdr

entries.name: cdar
entries.desc: Equivalent to (cdr (car x)).
entries.returns: The cdr of the car of x; an error when x or its car is not a pair.

entries.name: cddr
entries.desc: Equivalent to (cdr (cdr x)).
entries.returns: x without its first two elements; an error when x or its cdr is not a pair.

entries.name: list-tail
entries.desc: The list without its first k elements.
entries.returns: The k-th tail of list (shared, not copied); an error when k is not a non-negative fixnum or the list has fewer than k elements.

entries.name: memv
entries.desc: First tail whose car is eqv? to x, or #f.
entries.returns: The first tail of list whose car is eqv? to x (numbers compare by value and exactness), or #f; #f also when list is not a list.

entries.name: assv
entries.desc: First pair whose car is eqv? to key, or #f.
entries.returns: The first pair of alist whose car is eqv? to key, or #f; elements that are not pairs are skipped.

entries.name: cdddr
entries.desc: (cdr (cdr (cdr x))): x without its first three elements.
entries.returns: The third tail of x; an error "list too short" when x has fewer than 3 pairs.

entries.name: cadddr
entries.desc: Fourth element: (car (cdddr x)).
entries.returns: The fourth element of x; an error "list too short" when x has fewer than 4 elements.

entries.name: cddddr
entries.desc: (cdr (cdddr x)): x without its first four elements.
entries.returns: The fourth tail of x; an error "list too short" when x has fewer than 4 pairs.

entries.name: assoc
entries.desc: First pair of alist whose car is equal? to key, or #f.
entries.returns: The first pair whose car is equal? to key (strings and lists compare by content), or #f; elements that are not pairs are skipped.

entries.name: assq
entries.desc: First pair of alist whose car is eq? to key, or #f.
entries.returns: The first pair whose car is eq? to key (identity: use for symbols, small integers, booleans), or #f.

entries.name: caddr
entries.desc: The third element.
entries.returns: The third element of list; an error "list too short" when it has fewer than 3 elements.

entries.name: for-each
entries.desc: Call proc on the elements in order, for effect.
entries.returns: Void; with several lists it stops at the end of the shortest. An error with no list or more than 4 lists, when proc is not a procedure, or when proc raises one.

entries.name: list-ref
entries.desc: The k-th element (0-based).
entries.returns: The element at index k; an error when k is not a non-negative fixnum or is not less than the length.
entries.example:
(list-ref '(a b c) 1)  ; => b
(list-ref '(a b c) 0)  ; => a
(list-ref '(a b c) 3)  ; => error: index out of range

entries.name: member
entries.desc: First tail of list whose car is equal? to obj, or #f.
entries.returns: The first tail whose car is equal? to obj (structural comparison), or #f; #f also when list is not a list.

entries.name: memq
entries.desc: First tail of list whose car is eq? to obj, or #f.
entries.returns: The first tail whose car is eq? to obj (identity: use for symbols, small integers, booleans), or #f.
entries.example:
(memq 'c '(a b c d))  ; => (c d)
(memq 'z '(a b))     ; => #f
(if (memq 'red '(red green)) 'known 'unknown)  ; => known

entries.name: list-sort
entries.desc: A new list sorted by (less? a b); stable.
entries.returns: A newly allocated list of the elements of list in ascending order according to less? (a stable merge sort: equal elements keep their order; list is not changed); `()` for `()`. An error when list is not a proper list, less? is not a procedure, or less? raises one.
entries.notes: The argument order is R6RS `(list-sort proc list)` and SRFI 132.

entries.name: list-index
entries.desc: Index of the first element satisfying pred, or #f.
entries.returns: The 0-based index of the first element for which pred returns a true value, or #f when none does; an error when list is not a list or pred raises one.

entries.name: vector?
entries.desc: Test if obj is a vector.
entries.returns: #t or #f.

entries.name: make-vector
entries.desc: Create vector of length k, filled with fill (default 0).
entries.returns: A new vector of k elements, all fill (0 when omitted); an error when k is not a non-negative fixnum.

entries.name: vector
entries.desc: Create vector containing the given elements.
entries.returns: A new vector of the arguments; `#()` with no arguments.

entries.name: vector-length
entries.desc: Return the number of elements in vec.
entries.returns: An exact integer; an error when vec is not a vector.

entries.name: vector-ref
entries.desc: Return element at index k (0-based) in vec.
entries.returns: The element at index k; an error when vec is not a vector, k is not a fixnum (flonums are refused), or k is outside 0..length-1.
entries.example:
(define v (vector 'a 'b 'c))
(vector-ref v 1)     ; => b
(vector-ref v 3)     ; => error: out of bounds

entries.name: vector-set!
entries.desc: Set element at index k in vec to obj.
entries.returns: Void; an error when vec is not a vector, k is not a fixnum in 0..length-1, or vec is a quoted literal in the read-only code image.
entries.example:
(define v (make-vector 3 0))
(vector-set! v 1 'x)
v                    ; => #(0 x 0)
(vector-set! v 3 'y) ; => error: out of bounds
entries.notes: Quoted literals of an app loaded from the read-only code image (XIP) cannot be modified: mutating one raises "cannot modify a literal constant". Mutate freshly allocated data (list, vector, cons, make-vector) instead.

entries.name: vector->list
entries.desc: Convert vector elements to a newly allocated list.
entries.returns: A new list of the elements in order; an error when vec is not a vector.

entries.name: list->vector
entries.desc: Convert list elements to a newly allocated vector.
entries.returns: A new vector of the elements in order. Not checked: a non-list gives `#()` and the tail of an improper list is dropped.

entries.name: vector-fill!
entries.desc: Set all elements of vec to fill.
entries.returns: Void; an error when vec is not a vector or is a quoted literal in the read-only code image.
entries.notes: Quoted literals of an app loaded from the read-only code image (XIP) cannot be modified: mutating one raises "cannot modify a literal constant". Mutate freshly allocated data (list, vector, cons, make-vector) instead.

entries.name: string?
entries.desc: Test if obj is a string.
entries.returns: #t or #f; symbols and characters (integers) are not strings.

entries.name: string-length
entries.desc: Return the length of str in bytes (UTF-8: a non-ASCII character counts 2-4).
entries.returns: An exact integer, the number of bytes; an error when str is not a string.
entries.notes: Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions.

entries.name: string-ref
entries.desc: Return the byte at byte index k of str as an integer (a character code).
entries.returns: An integer 0..255 (for ASCII the character code: `(string-ref "abc" 0)` is 97 = `#\a`); an error when str is not a string, k not a fixnum, or k outside 0..length-1.
entries.notes: Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions. MiniScheme has no separate character type: a character is its integer code. `#\a` reads as 97, and `write` prints characters as integers.

entries.name: string-append
entries.desc: Concatenate strings into a new string.
entries.returns: A new string; `""` with no arguments; an error when an argument is not a string (convert numbers with `number->string`).

entries.name: substring
entries.desc: Return the bytes [start, end) of str as a new string.
entries.returns: A new string of end - start bytes; an error when str is not a string, start or end is not a fixnum (end is required), or not 0 <= start <= end <= length.
entries.notes: Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions. Cutting inside a multi-byte character gives invalid UTF-8.

entries.name: symbol->string
entries.desc: Convert symbol to string.
entries.returns: A new string of the symbol name; an error when sym is not a symbol.

entries.name: string->symbol
entries.desc: Convert string to interned symbol.
entries.returns: The interned symbol named str (eq? to the same name written literally); an error when str is not a string.

entries.name: string->number
entries.desc: Parse a number from str (radix 10 by default; #x #b #o #d prefixes), or return #f if invalid.
entries.returns: An exact integer (bignum when large), a flonum for decimal notation with "." or an exponent (radix 10 only), or #f when str is not a whole number (no surrounding text, no rationals); an error when str is not a string.
entries.notes: Leading whitespace is accepted only by the flonum parser: `(string->number " 12")` gives 12.0, `"12 "` gives #f.

entries.name: number->string
entries.desc: Convert number to string; integers in radix (default 10), flonums with up to 6 significant digits.
entries.returns: A new string. Integers are exact in any radix 2..36; flonums use C "%g": 6 significant digits and no ".0" (`2.0` gives "2"). An error when num is not a number.
entries.notes: For a fixed number of decimals, scale and round an integer, or format with `string->fixed` on input.

entries.name: list->string
entries.desc: Convert a list of byte values (character codes 0..255) to a string.
entries.returns: A new string with one byte per element. Not checked: values are truncated to their low byte, non-integer elements become NUL bytes, and a non-list gives "".
entries.notes: Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions. MiniScheme has no separate character type: a character is its integer code. `#\a` reads as 97, and `write` prints characters as integers.

entries.name: string->list
entries.desc: Convert a string to the list of its bytes (character codes 0..255).
entries.returns: A new list of integers 0..255, one per byte; an error when str is not a string.
entries.notes: Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions. MiniScheme has no separate character type: a character is its integer code. `#\a` reads as 97, and `write` prints characters as integers.

entries.name: string->ints
entries.desc: Integers of a comma-separated string: (string->ints "12,-3,7") => (12 -3 7). Reads the series fields sent by the app proxy.
entries.returns: A list of exact integers, at most 160 of them, bignums past the fixnum range. Spaces around fields are skipped, a field keeps its leading signed digits (up to 15) and fields without digits are dropped; an error when str is not a string.

entries.name: string->fixed
entries.desc: Leading decimal number of str times 10^digits as an integer: (string->fixed "12.3 %" 1) => 123.
entries.returns: An exact integer, rounded half up on the next digit, or #f when str (after leading spaces) does not start with a number; "." or "," separates decimals and trailing text is ignored. digits defaults to 0; an error when str is not a string or digits is outside 0..9. Allocates no flonum.

entries.name: string=?
entries.desc: String equality: all arguments have the same bytes.
entries.returns: #t or #f; an error with fewer than 2 arguments or when an argument is not a string.

entries.name: string<?
entries.desc: Lexicographic byte order: each argument is less than the next.
entries.returns: #t or #f, comparing bytes (case-sensitive: "B" < "a"; a proper prefix is less); an error with fewer than 2 arguments or a non-string.

entries.name: string>?
entries.desc: Lexicographic byte order: each argument is greater than the next.
entries.returns: #t or #f, comparing bytes as for `string<?`; an error with fewer than 2 arguments or a non-string.

entries.name: string-split
entries.desc: The pieces of str between occurrences of sep.
entries.returns: A list of new strings: the bytes of str between non-overlapping occurrences of sep, scanned from the left. sep is a non-empty string or a character (byte value). Adjacent separators give empty strings; `("")` for "". An error when str is not a string or sep is empty or of another type.
entries.notes: Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions.

entries.name: string-join
entries.desc: Concatenate strings with sep between them.
entries.returns: A new string: the elements of the list strings with sep (default " ") between consecutive ones; "" for `()`. An error when strings is not a list of strings or sep is not a string.

entries.name: string-trim
entries.desc: str without leading and trailing whitespace.
entries.returns: A new string without the leading and trailing ASCII whitespace bytes (space, tab, LF, CR, VT, FF); other bytes are kept. An error when str is not a string.

entries.name: string-index
entries.desc: Byte index of the first sub at or after start, or #f.
entries.returns: The byte offset in str of the first occurrence of sub (a string, or a character byte value) that begins at or after start (default 0), or #f; an empty sub gives start. An error when start is not in 0..length or an argument has the wrong type.
entries.notes: Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions. The result can be passed to `substring`.

entries.name: string-upcase
entries.desc: ASCII letters to upper case.
entries.returns: A new string with a-z changed to A-Z; every other byte (including UTF-8 sequences) unchanged. An error when str is not a string.

entries.name: string-downcase
entries.desc: ASCII letters to lower case.
entries.returns: A new string with A-Z changed to a-z; every other byte (including UTF-8 sequences) unchanged. An error when str is not a string.

entries.name: string-prefix?
entries.desc: Whether str starts with prefix.
entries.returns: #t when the first bytes of str equal prefix (always #t for ""), else #f; an error when an argument is not a string.

entries.name: string-suffix?
entries.desc: Whether str ends with suffix.
entries.returns: #t when the last bytes of str equal suffix (always #t for ""), else #f; an error when an argument is not a string.

entries.name: string-pad-left
entries.desc: str padded on the left to n characters.
entries.returns: A new string of exactly n bytes: str preceded by copies of char (a byte value, default #\space) when shorter, or its last n bytes when longer. An error when n is not a non-negative fixnum or char is not 0..255.
entries.notes: Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions. Meant for ASCII text such as clock digits.

entries.name: char->integer
entries.desc: Return the code of char; characters are already integers, so this is the identity.
entries.returns: The integer itself (`#\A` is 65); an error when char is not a fixnum.
entries.notes: MiniScheme has no separate character type: a character is its integer code. `#\a` reads as 97, and `write` prints characters as integers.

entries.name: integer->char
entries.desc: Return the character with code k; characters are integers, so this is the identity.
entries.returns: k itself (written as an integer); an error when k is not a fixnum.
entries.notes: MiniScheme has no separate character type: a character is its integer code. `#\a` reads as 97, and `write` prints characters as integers.

entries.name: char=?
entries.desc: Character equality: all codes are equal.
entries.returns: #t or #f; an error with fewer than 2 arguments or when an argument is not a fixnum (character).
entries.notes: MiniScheme has no separate character type: a character is its integer code. `#\a` reads as 97, and `write` prints characters as integers.

entries.name: char<?
entries.desc: Character order: each code is less than the next.
entries.returns: #t or #f by code; an error with fewer than 2 arguments or a non-fixnum.

entries.name: char>?
entries.desc: Character order: each code is greater than the next.
entries.returns: #t or #f by code; an error with fewer than 2 arguments or a non-fixnum.

entries.name: char<=?
entries.desc: Character order: each code is less than or equal to the next.
entries.returns: #t or #f by code; an error with fewer than 2 arguments or a non-fixnum.

entries.name: char>=?
entries.desc: Character order: each code is greater than or equal to the next.
entries.returns: #t or #f by code; an error with fewer than 2 arguments or a non-fixnum.

entries.name: api-version
entries.desc: The API version this firmware provides, "major.minor.patch".
entries.returns: A string such as "1.0.0". Never fails.

entries.name: api-compatible?
entries.desc: Whether an app needing API `required` ("1.0") runs here: same major, minor not higher.
entries.returns: #t or #f. `required` is "M", "M.m" or "M.m.p" (the patch level never matters); text that is not a version gives #f; an error when required is not a string.

entries.name: api-has?
entries.desc: Whether this device provides the procedure (a symbol or string): known to the API, not reserved, its extension present.
entries.returns: #t or #f: #f for unknown and reserved names, for names of an extension the device lacks, and for names not bound here (device-only names in the PC REPL). Older names count like their current name; special forms are #t. An error when name is not a symbol or string.

entries.name: api-info
entries.desc: What the API table says about a name: (component since status extension where), or #f.
entries.returns: A list ("component" "since" status extension where): status is the symbol stable, reserved or alias; extension is the extension id string or #f; where is all, device or pc. #f for a name the API does not know; an error when name is not a symbol or string.
entries.example:
(api-info 'gpio-write) ; => ("gpio" "1.0.0" stable #f all)
(api-info 'millis) ; => ("time" "1.0.0" alias #f all)
(api-info 'i2c-open) ; => ("i2c" "1.0.0" reserved #f all)
(api-info 'no-such-thing) ; => #f

entries.name: api-list
entries.desc: Names of the API (of one component), as strings.
entries.returns: A list of strings in alphabetical order, including reserved entries and older names (check them with api-has? / api-info). An unknown component gives (); an error when component is not a symbol or string.

entries.name: api-components
entries.desc: The component ids, as strings.
entries.returns: A list of strings in reference order, the language core first ("syntax" "math" ...). Never fails.

entries.name: api-extensions
entries.desc: The extension APIs on this device: (("esp32" . "1.0.0") ...).
entries.returns: An alist of (id . version) strings; () on a host without extensions (the PC REPL). The firmware and the WASM simulator report (("esp32" . "1.0.0")).
entries.example:
(define esp32-api (assoc "esp32" (api-extensions)))   ; ("esp32" . "1.0.0") on the board
(if esp32-api (cdr esp32-api) "none")

entries.name: sys-restart
entries.desc: Reboot the board at once (the REPL reports a timeout; the file manager's restart replies first). Not for apps: only the system settings and the REPL may (an app gets an error).
entries.returns: Does not return on the board (esp_restart). The WASM simulator raises the error "restart: the simulated device is rebooting" and reboots the simulated device; the PC REPL resets its mock pins and files and returns void.
entries.example:
(config-set! "system" "boot_app" "apps/weather.msbc")
(sys-restart)   ; the board boots the weather app

entries.name: sys-chip-model
entries.desc: The chip model as a string: model, revision and cores ("ESP32 rev1.0 2C").
entries.returns: A string: "ESP32 rev<major>.<minor> <cores>C" on the board, "ESP32 (WASM simulator)" in the simulator, "PC-Mock-ESP32-Virtual" in the PC REPL. Never fails.

entries.name: sys-chip-info
entries.desc: Alist describing the chip, the firmware build and the flash.
entries.returns: An alist. On the board: (model . "ESP32") (revision . n) (cores . n) (cpu-mhz . n) (wifi-bt . "WiFi+BT") (mac . "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF") (idf . "v6.1") (build . "Oct 10 2026") (reset-reason . "power-on") (flash-bytes . n) (app-image-bytes . n) (app-partition-bytes . n) and, with the file system mounted, (spiffs-bytes . n) (spiffs-used . n). reset-reason is one of "unknown" "power-on" "external" "software" "panic" "int-watchdog" "task-watchdog" "watchdog" "deep-sleep" "brownout" "sdio". The simulator gives the same keys; the PC REPL only model, cores and flash-bytes. Never fails.
entries.example:
(define chip (sys-chip-info))
(cdr (assq 'flash-bytes chip)) ; => 4194304
(assq 'reset-reason chip)   ; (reset-reason . "power-on") on the board after power-up

entries.name: sys-info
entries.desc: Nested alist of system figures (memory, flash, network, time, VM).
entries.returns: An alist of sections (chip memory flash network time display peripherals), each an alist: chip is sys-chip-info; memory has free-heap largest-block min-free total vm-used vm-heap app-rom stack-depth frame-depth; flash has total app-image app-partition app-rom app-rom-partition; network has connected ssid ip rssi; time has ntp-synced uptime-ms; display has model width height mode band-lines color-bits color-scheme color buffer-bytes dma-buffer-bytes; peripherals has backlight light-adc light-lux ws2812 button. Never fails.
entries.example:
(map car (sys-info)) ; => (chip memory flash network time display peripherals)
(define (info section key) (cdr (assq key (cdr (assq section (sys-info))))))
(info 'flash 'total) ; => 4194304
(info 'memory 'free-heap)   ; free system RAM, about 33000 on the board

entries.name: mem-free
entries.desc: Free system RAM in bytes (the C heap outside the VM heap: WiFi, HTTP, buffers).
entries.returns: An integer (esp_get_free_heap_size; about 33000 on the reference board while an app runs). The simulator reports a fixed 15076, the PC REPL 4194304. Never fails.

entries.name: mem-total
entries.desc: Internal RAM managed by the system heap, in bytes.
entries.returns: An integer (heap_caps_get_total_size of internal RAM, about 300 KB on the ESP32); the simulator and the PC REPL report 323584 (316 KB). Never fails.

entries.name: mem-min-free
entries.desc: The lowest free system heap since boot, in bytes.
entries.returns: An integer (esp_get_minimum_free_heap_size): the low-water mark, never above mem-free. The simulator reports a fixed 2788, the PC REPL 12288. Never fails.
entries.example:
(define headroom (mem-min-free))   ; 14000..19000 on the board under load
(if (< headroom 8192) (display "the system heap ran low"))

entries.name: mem-max-block
entries.desc: Largest free system heap block in bytes: the biggest single C allocation that can succeed now.
entries.returns: An integer (heap_caps_get_largest_free_block of 8-bit capable RAM); the simulator reports a fixed 10240, the PC REPL 28672. Never fails.

entries.name: mem-report
entries.desc: Alist of the system heap figures and the free stack of the firmware tasks; collects the VM heap first.
entries.returns: An alist of integers: (free-heap . n) (min-free-heap . n) (largest-block . n) (vm-heap . n) (vm-live . n) after a full VM collection, then (stack-free:<task> . bytes) for each running task of main, httpd, jsonfeed, mirror_stream, market, tiT, wifi, sys_evt, esp_timer, ipc0, ipc1, IDLE0, IDLE1, Tmr Svc (the stack high-water mark). Firmware only: the WASM simulator does not provide it.

entries.name: flash-total-bytes
entries.desc: Flash chip size in bytes.
entries.returns: An integer: 4194304 (4 MB) on the reference board and in the simulator. Never fails.

entries.name: flash-app-bytes
entries.desc: Size of the running firmware image in bytes.
entries.returns: An integer: the verified image length of the running partition (the first call hashes the image, later calls use the cached figure); 0 when the image cannot be verified. The simulator and the PC REPL report 1078192. Never fails.
entries.example:
(< (flash-app-bytes) (flash-app-partition-bytes)) ; => #t
(- (flash-app-partition-bytes) (flash-app-bytes))   ; room left for a larger firmware

entries.name: flash-app-partition-bytes
entries.desc: Size of the partition the firmware runs from, in bytes.
entries.returns: An integer: 1572864 (the 1536 KB factory partition) on the reference board and in the simulator; 0 when the running partition is unknown. Never fails.

entries.name: power-deep-sleep
entries.desc: Deep sleep for ms milliseconds; the board then reboots.
entries.returns: Does not return on the board: everything but the RTC stops, and the timer wakes the chip, which boots afresh (reset reason "deep-sleep"; RAM and the VM are lost). ms must be a positive integer; otherwise nothing happens and void is returned. The WASM simulator returns void at once; the PC REPL blocks for ms.
entries.notes: The display, WiFi and the LED stay off while the chip sleeps; the boot app starts again on wake.

entries.name: power-light-sleep
entries.desc: Pause the CPU for ms with RAM and WiFi kept.
entries.returns: The wake cause as a symbol: timer after ms, button when KEY 18 was pressed first. RAM, the VM, the panel contents and the WiFi association are kept (traffic waits until the wake). An error when ms is not a positive integer.

entries.name: power-battery-mv
entries.desc: Battery voltage in millivolts, or #f without a battery.
entries.returns: An integer in millivolts read through the board's battery divider (calibrated ADC), or #f on a board without battery sensing (the reference board). Never fails.

entries.name: time-sleep-ms
entries.desc: Pause the app for ms milliseconds; the app loop (display, button) waits too.
entries.returns: Void. On the board the task yields for ms (1 ms tick); ms <= 0 or a non-integer does nothing. The WASM simulator returns at once without waiting.
entries.notes: Long pauses freeze the screen and the button; apps should do periodic work in the app-tick or app-step hooks instead.

entries.name: time-sleep-us
entries.desc: Busy-wait for us microseconds (short, precise delays).
entries.returns: Void. The CPU spins for us (esp_rom_delay_us) without yielding; us <= 0 or a non-integer does nothing. The WASM simulator returns at once.

entries.name: time-ms
entries.desc: Milliseconds since boot (the page load in the simulator).
entries.returns: An exact integer, never negative or wrapped: a bignum past the fixnum range (2^28 ms, about 3.1 days of uptime, on 32-bit targets). Never fails.

entries.name: time-us
entries.desc: Microseconds since boot, for timing short intervals.
entries.returns: An exact integer, never negative or wrapped: a bignum past the fixnum range (2^28 us, about 4.5 minutes, on 32-bit targets; reading a bignum allocates a few bytes). Never fails.
entries.example:
(define t0 (time-us))
(define x (expt 3 40))
(- (time-us) t0)   ; microseconds the computation took

entries.name: time-synced?
entries.desc: Whether the wall clock has been set (NTP).
entries.returns: #t once SNTP has set the clock (time after November 2023), #f before. The simulator and the PC REPL use the host clock and give #t. Never fails.
entries.notes: The firmware syncs from ntp.aliyun.com and cn.pool.ntp.org once WiFi is up; the local time zone is CST-8. The app-tick hook receives the wall time each second.

entries.name: time-epoch
entries.desc: Seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC, or #f before the clock is set.
entries.returns: An exact integer (a bignum on 32-bit targets, where fixnums end at 2^28), or #f while time-synced? is #f. Never fails.

entries.name: time-local
entries.desc: The local time: (year month day hour minute second weekday), or #f.
entries.returns: A list of 7 integers in the device's time zone: month 1..12, day 1..31, hour 0..23, weekday 0..6 with 0 = Sunday; #f while the clock is not synced. Never fails.
entries.notes: The wall time of the last app-tick (once a second), so it can lag the clock by up to a second. Use it for the year, or to count days (an every-other-day plan). Check it with (defined? 'time-local) on older firmware.

entries.name: time-utc-offset
entries.desc: Offset of the local time zone from UTC in seconds.
entries.returns: An integer, seconds east of UTC at the current time (daylight saving included): 28800 for "CST-8", the firmware default. Never fails.

entries.name: time-set-zone!
entries.desc: Set the local time zone (POSIX TZ string such as "CST-8").
entries.returns: #t; the zone applies at once to time-local, time-utc-offset and the app-tick wall time and is kept in config.ini [system] timezone for the next boot. An error when tz is not a string or not a valid POSIX TZ string.

entries.name: app-rom-capacity
entries.desc: Bytes of the approm flash partition that holds the app's Code ROM image (vm-rom-bytes is the image); 0 when there is none.
entries.returns: An integer: 262144 (one 256 KB slot of the approm partition: 512 KB in two slots since firmware 1.0.71) on the reference board, in the simulator and the PC REPL; 0 on a firmware whose partition table has no approm. Never fails.

entries.name: app-last-stats
entries.desc: Figures of the app that ran before the system settings opened (kept across that restart), or #f.
entries.returns: #f when no app was recorded (after power-up), else an alist: (id . "weather") (heap . n) (live . n) (peak . n) (rom . n) (uptime-s . n) (free-heap . n) (min-free . n) in bytes and seconds, plus (phase . rom|load|crash) (error . "text") when the app failed. Kept in RTC RAM: survives a restart, not a power cycle. The simulator reports 0 for uptime-s, free-heap and min-free.
entries.example:
(define s (app-last-stats))
(if s (cdr (assq 'peak s)) 0)        ; e.g. 61240: the app's peak live VM heap
(and s (assq 'error s))              ; e.g. (error . "car: expected a pair")

entries.name: app-info
entries.desc: The running app: (path id ini-path folder).
entries.returns: A list of four strings: the app image, its id (from its metadata, else its folder), its settings file <folder>/config.ini and its folder (/spiffs/apps/<id> or /spiffs/user/<id>, where its files go). In the system settings: id "settings". Never fails.

entries.name: app-list
entries.desc: The installed apps with their metadata: ((path id name description pages version) ...).
entries.returns: A list with one list per app: path, id, name (the id when the metadata has none), description and version are strings ("" when missing), pages an integer (1 when missing). The apps of /spiffs/apps/<id>/ (the market) and /spiffs/user/<id>/ (uploaded) come first, then the built-in /spiffs/app.msbc unless the same id is installed from the market; never the system settings; at most 16 apps. () when none. Never fails.

entries.name: app-scheduled
entries.desc: The time this run is for, "HH:MM": a launch from the app's schedule.ini, or the time its app-schedule hook was called with; #f otherwise.
entries.returns: A string "HH:MM" or #f. Never fails.
entries.notes: An app with schedule.ini in its folder ([schedule] times = 08:00, 12:30, 19:00) is started by the system at those times (wall clock, once synced): the board restarts into it, and (app-scheduled) tells it why it runs. When the app is already running at such a time it is not restarted: its app-schedule hook, (define (app-schedule at) ...), is called with the time instead (no hook: nothing happens). Several apps due at the same time run one after another. A scheduled launch stays until it calls (app-return), or for return_after seconds when its schedule.ini sets it. The app (or its web page, through /api/app/file?name=schedule.ini) writes schedule.ini itself.

entries.name: app-return
entries.desc: A scheduled launch is done: the next app due at that time, else the boot app, starts after this call (#t); #f when there is nothing to return to.
entries.returns: #t when a restart follows (within a second; the app keeps running until then), #f when this run is not a scheduled launch and no other launch waits. Clears (app-scheduled) then. Never fails.
entries.notes: The boot app ([system] boot_app) is the app the board ran before the launch. An app that handled its app-schedule hook while running as the boot app calls (app-return) too: other apps due at the same time wait for it, then run (#t); with none waiting it stays (#f).

entries.name: config-get
entries.desc: Value of a key in the running app's own config.ini (its folder), else in /spiffs/config.ini, as a string; #f when neither has it. app-id: a member of the running combined app.
entries.returns: A string (trimmed, comment removed, at most 159 bytes) or #f. The key is matched without case in any section; the first match wins. An error when key is not a string.
entries.notes: An app's defaults ([config] of its metadata) are written to its config.ini when it first runs, so config-get finds them there; the settings web page edits the same file. An app gets no secrets of config.ini: wifi_* keys, boot_app and keys containing password, passwd, secret or token answer #f (the system settings and the REPL get them). Since 1.6.0 a combined app (meta [combo] members = a, b) passes a member's id to read that app's own config.ini (apps/<id>/, else user/<id>/); another id is an error. Firmware before 1.6.0 ignores app-id.

entries.name: app-has-config?
entries.desc: Whether a member of the running combined app ([combo] members) has its own config.ini.
entries.returns: #t or #f. An error when app-id is not a member of the running combined app.
entries.notes: A member that never ran on its own and was never set up has no config.ini: the combined app then uses the defaults of that member's metadata. Check it with (defined? 'app-has-config?) on older firmware.

entries.name: app-member-folder
entries.desc: Make the relative file paths of the running combined app's code those of member app-id's own folder (apps/<id>), #f: its own again.
entries.returns: #t. An error when app-id is neither #f nor a member of the running combined app ([combo] members).
entries.example:
(app-member-folder "medicine")   ; => #t   (fs-read "meds.txt") reads apps/medicine/meds.txt now
(app-member-folder #f)           ; => #t   back to the combined app's folder
entries.notes: The storage quota is the member's too (its meta's storage_kb, as when it runs alone), and the folder is made when missing. combo.scm switches around each member's code (also while it loads), so a member shares its files with the app running alone; (app-info) names that folder meanwhile. Since 1.13.0 a time of a member's schedule.ini that comes while the combined app runs is not a launch of the member: the combined app's app-schedule hook is called with the time and the member's id, (app-schedule at id).

entries.name: config-set!
entries.desc: Write key = value into /spiffs/config.ini (the line replaced in place with its comment kept, else added to [section]); #t when saved. Read again at the next boot.
entries.returns: #t when the file was written, #f when it could not be (out of memory, file system full). Most settings take effect at the next boot. An error when section, key or value is not a string.
entries.notes: An existing key is found in any section and replaced where it is; the file is rewritten through a temporary file. Values are stored as text: pass numbers with number->string. Not for apps: only the system settings and the REPL may (an app gets an error). An app keeps its own settings with app-config-set!.

entries.name: app-config-set!
entries.desc: Store a setting in the running app's own config.ini ([config] section, in its folder).
entries.returns: #t when saved, #f when the file could not be written. config-get reads it back at once. An error when key or value is not a string.

entries.name: setup-mode-start
entries.desc: Start the setup access point and its web page. Not for apps: only the system settings and the REPL may (an app gets an error).
entries.returns: (ssid ip) strings of the open access point, such as ("MiniScheme-A1B2" "192.168.4.1"), or #f when it could not start. Starting it again returns the running one. A station that is not connected stops retrying while the access point runs.
entries.notes: The access point has no password; a captive DNS sends every name to the setup page, which edits WiFi and config.ini settings.

entries.name: factory-reset
entries.desc: Reset part of the board from the system settings: 'rom (the app Code ROM partition), 'configs (the apps' /spiffs/apps/<id>.ini), 'fonts (the system font ROM), 'files (every file: apps, data, config.ini, WiFi) or 'all (the Code ROM and every file; the font ROM stays).
entries.returns: #t, and the board restarts 1.5 s later into the built-in system settings (never a copy from the market); a string saying why when it cannot ("factory-reset: only in the system settings"). A symbol other than the five is an error.
entries.notes: Holding KEY 18 from power-on for 10 s (config.ini [system] factory_reset_key = 1) erases the Code ROM and opens the built-in settings too. After 'files or 'all the firmware writes a default config.ini on the next boot; WiFi has to be set up again (setup mode).

entries.name: setup-mode-status
entries.desc: The state of setup mode and the WiFi station, as an alist.
entries.returns: An alist: (ap . #t/#f) (ap-ssid . "MiniScheme-A1B2") (ap-ip . "192.168.4.1") (clients . n) (sta-connected . #t/#f) (sta-ssid . "...") (sta-ip . "...") (saved . n), where clients counts the phones joined to the access point and saved the settings saved from the page since boot. Never fails.
entries.example:
(define st (setup-mode-status))
(cdr (assq 'clients st))   ; phones joined to the setup hotspot
(cdr (assq 'sta-connected st))

entries.name: market-refresh
entries.desc: Start reading the market index in the background; (market-status) follows it, (market-apps) has the result.
entries.returns: #t when the read started; otherwise a string saying why ("market: busy", "market: not connected", "market: no market_url and no proxy in config.ini"). Never an error.
entries.notes: The market is `config.ini [market] market_url`, else `<[app] proxy>/market` (the app proxy, minischeme-proxy, serves its apps/ folder there). Its index.json lists every app with id, name, description, version, api, extensions, file, size and hash (FNV-1a of the image). The board fetches over plain HTTP. Automatic updates (`[market] market_auto_update = 1`): an app's boot checks once when the network comes up (within 30 s); with updates the device restarts into the system settings, installs them and restarts into the app. No network at boot or a failed check: skipped until the next boot, never retried.

entries.name: market-status
entries.desc: What the market does now: an alist of state, message, app, received, total, queued, install, auto, return and url.
entries.returns: ((state . s) (message . str) (app . id-or-#f) (received . bytes) (total . bytes) (queued . n) (install . #t/#f) (auto . a) (return . #t/#f) (url . str)); state is idle, refreshing, installing or error; message is the last outcome in English ("5 apps, 1 updates", "weather 2 installed", "auto update: 1 installed, 0 failed"); install: whether installs may run now (on the board only in the system settings); auto: the automatic round of this boot, off, check (an app's boot check) or update (the settings installing the updates it found); return: that round is over and the settings go back to the app. Never an error.
entries.example:
(define st (market-status))
(cdr (assq 'state st))      ; => installing
(cdr (assq 'app st))        ; => "weather"
(quotient (* 100 (cdr (assq 'received st))) (max 1 (cdr (assq 'total st))))   ; percent

entries.name: market-apps
entries.desc: The apps of the last index read, each compared with the installed copy.
entries.returns: A list of (id name version installed status size description): installed is the installed copy's version or #f; status is new, installed (same image), update (another image, not an older version) or incompatible (needs a newer API or an extension this device lacks). () before a refresh.

entries.name: market-install
entries.desc: Queue the install of an app (a string id), or 'updates for every app with an update; downloads run in the background.
entries.returns: The number of apps queued; a string saying why when none is ("market: install and update apps in the system settings" while an app runs on the board, "market: no app x", "market: no updates", "market: refresh the list first", or an incompatible app). Never an error. Each image goes to a temporary file, is checked (size, hash, image, API) and only then replaces the installed file (/spiffs/apps/<id>.msbc, or the root app.msbc when that is the installed copy); the apps run the new version from the next boot.
entries.example:
(market-refresh)
;; ... once (market-status) says idle:
(market-install "weather")    ; => 1
(market-install 'updates)     ; => 2, or "market: no updates"

entries.name: market-cancel
entries.desc: Stop the read or download in progress and empty the install queue; the installed files are untouched.

entries.name: bench-tick
entries.desc: Average time of n synthetic clock ticks with a partial redraw to the LCD; diagnostic.
entries.returns: An alist of averages per tick: (tick-us . n) (alloc-bytes . n) (minor-gcs . total). n is clamped to 1..600, default 60; the screen is repainted afterwards. Firmware only: the WASM simulator does not provide it.
entries.notes: Runs the app-tick hook with fixed times (14:00:01 ...): the app shows them until its next real tick.

entries.name: bench-display
entries.desc: Time n renders of the screen (or rows y..y+h) through the LCD path; diagnostic.
entries.returns: An alist of averages per pass: (full-render-us . n) (lcd-us . n) (alloc-bytes . n). n is clamped to 1..600, default 10. With replay? true the recorded drawing is replayed instead of re-running the render procedure (the cost of a scrolling-text frame). Firmware only: the WASM simulator does not provide it.

entries.name: gpio-mode
entries.desc: Set a pin's mode: 0 or 'input, 1 or 'output, 2 or 'pullup (also 'input-pullup): input with pull-up.
entries.returns: Void. Never raises an error: a non-integer pin is ignored, other numbers and unknown symbols mean output. On the board pins of the display bus (2 4 12-17 25-27 32 33) are left alone, and 34..39 are input only.
entries.example:
(gpio-mode 5 'output)
(gpio-mode 19 'pullup)   ; a switch from GPIO 19 to GND
(gpio-mode 34 0)         ; input
entries.notes: Free pins on the reference board: 0, 5, 19, 23 (in/out) and 34, 36, 39 (input only). KEY 18, the LED (21), the backlight (22) and the light sensor (35) have their own procedures.

entries.name: gpio-write
entries.desc: Set the output level of a pin: 0 low, any other integer high.
entries.returns: Void. Never raises an error: non-integer arguments are ignored; on the board pins of the display bus are left alone. Set the pin to output with gpio-mode first.

entries.name: gpio-read
entries.desc: Read the input level of a pin (0 or 1).
entries.returns: 0 or 1; 0 when pin is not an integer. A pin set to output reads back the level last written (on the board its input stays enabled).

entries.name: gpio-toggle
entries.desc: Invert an output pin.
entries.returns: The new level, 0 or 1. An error when pin is not an output-capable pin (0..33) set to output by gpio-mode, or belongs to the display bus.

entries.name: gpio-on-change
entries.desc: Call (proc pin level) from the app loop when the pin changes; edge is 'rising, 'falling or 'both.
entries.returns: #t. The interrupt only records the edge; proc runs from the app loop on its next pass, once per pass however many edges came (level is the level then). A new call for the same pin replaces its watcher; watchers end with the app. An error when pin is not 0..39, edge is not one of the three symbols or proc is not a procedure.

entries.name: gpio-off-change
entries.desc: Stop watching a pin.
entries.returns: #t when a watcher was removed, #f when the pin had none. An error when pin is not an integer.

entries.name: adc-read
entries.desc: Raw 12-bit reading (0..4095) of an analog input pin.
entries.returns: An integer 0..4095 (12 bits, 0..about 3.3 V at the default 12 dB attenuation) for the ADC1 pins 32..39; 0 for other pins or a non-integer pin. The simulator returns the light sensor for pin 35 and 2048 for the other ADC1 pins.
entries.example:
(define raw (adc-read 34))
(quotient (* raw 3300) 4095)   ; rough millivolts at 11 dB attenuation
entries.notes: ADC1 pins are 32..39 (34, 36 and 39 are free on the reference board); ADC2 cannot be used while WiFi runs.

entries.name: adc-read-mv
entries.desc: Calibrated input voltage in millivolts.
entries.returns: An integer in millivolts, corrected with the chip's eFuse calibration for the pin's attenuation (11 dB by default: about 150..2450 mV). An error when pin is not an ADC1 pin (32..39).

entries.name: adc-config
entries.desc: Input range of an analog pin: attenuation 0, 2.5, 6 or 11 dB.
entries.returns: #t. Full-scale ranges: 0 dB about 950 mV, 2.5 dB 1250 mV, 6 dB 1750 mV, 11 dB 2450 mV (the default). An error when pin is not an ADC1 pin (32..39) or the attenuation is not one of the four.

entries.name: dac-write
entries.desc: Output a voltage: value 0..255 of the supply.
entries.returns: #t; the pin then holds value / 255 x 3.3 V until the next call. An error when pin is not a DAC pin (25 or 26 on the ESP32) or is in use (on the reference board both drive the display bus), or value is not 0..255.

entries.name: pwm-write
entries.desc: PWM output on a pin: frequency in Hz and duty cycle 0..255.
entries.returns: Void. Never raises an error: non-integer arguments are ignored, duty is clamped to 0..255. On the board each pin gets one of 7 LEDC channels on a shared timer (the latest freq applies to all of them; freq <= 0 means 5000 Hz); pins of the display bus are left alone and pin 22 sets the backlight, as in the simulator (use backlight-set for that).

entries.name: pwm-config
entries.desc: Frequency and resolution of a PWM pin.
entries.returns: #t. resolution-bits is 1..16 (default 8) and freq-hz x 2^bits must not exceed 80 MHz; pwm-write's duty then ranges 0..2^bits - 1 on that pin. An error when the pin is not output-capable or belongs to the display bus, the combination is not possible, or no PWM channel is free (7 are; the backlight uses one).
entries.example:
(pwm-config 23 50 14)        ; servo: 50 Hz, 14 bits
(pwm-write 23 50 1229)       ; 1.5 ms pulse: centre

entries.name: pwm-stop
entries.desc: Stop PWM on a pin and release its channel.
entries.returns: #t when PWM ran on the pin (now driven low), #f when it had none. An error when pin is not an integer.

entries.name: i2c-open
entries.desc: Start an I2C master on two pins.
entries.returns: #t. port is 0 or 1; freq-hz defaults to 100000 (up to 1000000); the internal pull-ups are enabled. An error when the port is already open or not 0/1, or a pin is not output-capable or belongs to the display bus.

entries.name: i2c-close
entries.desc: Release an I2C port.
entries.returns: #t when the port was open, #f otherwise. Ports close when the app ends.

entries.name: i2c-scan
entries.desc: Addresses of the devices that answer.
entries.returns: A list of the 7-bit addresses (8..119) that acknowledge, ascending; () when none. An error when the port is not open.
entries.example:
(i2c-open 0 19 23)
(i2c-scan 0)   ; e.g. (60 118): an SSD1306 and a BME280

entries.name: i2c-write
entries.desc: Write bytes (a string or a list of integers) to a device.
entries.returns: #t when the device acknowledged every byte, #f when it did not answer (NAK or a 50 ms timeout). An error when the port is not open, addr is not 0..127 or a byte is not 0..255.

entries.name: i2c-read
entries.desc: Read n bytes from a device.
entries.returns: A list of n integers 0..255, or #f when the device did not answer. An error when the port is not open, addr is not 0..127 or n is not 1..256.
entries.example: (i2c-read 0 72 2)   ; e.g. (25 128): two bytes of a temperature sensor

entries.name: i2c-write-read
entries.desc: Write then read in one transaction (register reads).
entries.returns: A list of n integers 0..255 read after a repeated start, or #f when the device did not answer. Errors as i2c-write and i2c-read.

entries.name: spi-open
entries.desc: Start an SPI master.
entries.returns: #t. port is 2 (SPI2) or 3 (SPI3); miso -1 for write-only devices; freq-hz defaults to 1000000 (up to 26000000 through the GPIO matrix); mode 0..3, default 0. An error when the port is open already or invalid, or a pin is unusable or belongs to the display bus.

entries.name: spi-close
entries.desc: Release an SPI port.
entries.returns: #t when the port was open, #f otherwise. Ports close when the app ends.

entries.name: spi-transfer
entries.desc: Clock bytes out with chip select cs low; the bytes clocked in.
entries.returns: A list of integers 0..255, as many as were sent (all 0 without miso). bytes is a string or a list of integers 0..255, at most 4096; cs -1 leaves chip select to the app. An error when the port is not open or a byte is out of range.

entries.name: uart-open
entries.desc: Open a serial port.
entries.returns: #t. port is 1 or 2 (UART0 is the console and the REPL); 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit; a 1024-byte receive buffer. An error when the port is open already or invalid, a pin is unusable or baud is not 300..5000000.

entries.name: uart-close
entries.desc: Close a serial port.
entries.returns: #t when the port was open, #f otherwise. Ports close when the app ends.

entries.name: uart-write
entries.desc: Send a string or a list of bytes.
entries.returns: The number of bytes queued (an integer); waits only while the transmit buffer is full. An error when the port is not open or a byte is not 0..255.

entries.name: uart-read
entries.desc: The bytes received so far (a string, maybe empty).
entries.returns: A string of up to max bytes (default: all buffered) taken from the receive buffer; "" when nothing arrived. Never waits. An error when the port is not open.

entries.name: uart-available
entries.desc: Number of bytes waiting.
entries.returns: An integer 0..1024: the bytes in the receive buffer. An error when the port is not open.

entries.name: timer-start
entries.desc: Call (proc) from the app loop after ms (every ms when repeat?).
entries.returns: A timer id (a positive integer). proc runs on the first app-loop pass after it is due, never from an interrupt; a repeating timer that falls behind skips the missed calls. Timers end with the app. An error when ms is not a positive integer, proc is not a procedure or all 8 timers are in use.

entries.name: timer-stop
entries.desc: Cancel a timer.
entries.returns: #t when the timer was pending, #f when the id is unknown or a one-shot timer already ran.

entries.name: button-read
entries.desc: The user button (KEY 18) now: 1 pressed, 0 released.
entries.returns: 0 or 1. The firmware samples the button once per app-loop pass (a press shorter than a pass still counts once); the WebREPL's KEY 18 counts too. Never fails.
entries.notes: For presses use the hooks: app-button (short press), app-long-press (0.8 s), app-mid-press (3.5 s); an 8 s hold opens the hardware pages, where a mid press opens the system settings.
