Inside the system settings (since 1.3.0) the mid press reaches the settings app (back) and there is no hold. The times are config.ini [system] button_long_ms, button_mid_ms, button_hold_ms.

entries.name: button-pressed?
entries.desc: Whether the user button (KEY 18) is held now.
entries.returns: #t or #f, the same sample as button-read. Never fails.

entries.name: led-set
entries.desc: Set the RGB status LED (WS2812) color, each channel 0..255.
entries.returns: Void. Each value is taken modulo 256 (300 gives 44); with fewer than three integers nothing changes. Never raises an error.

entries.name: led-get
entries.desc: The LED color last set, as (r g b).
entries.returns: A list of three integers 0..255; (0 0 0) after boot. Never fails.

entries.name: led-clear
entries.desc: Turn the RGB status LED off.
entries.returns: Void; the same as (led-set 0 0 0). Never fails.

entries.name: light-read
entries.desc: Raw photoresistor reading (0..4095): higher is brighter.
entries.returns: An integer 0..4095: on the board a trimmed mean of 16 ADC samples of GPIO 35, refreshed every 3 s by the firmware (or the WebREPL's simulated value); 2048 until the first sample. Never fails.

entries.name: light-lux
entries.desc: Rough brightness 0..1000, scaled linearly from light-read; not a calibrated lux value.
entries.returns: An integer: (quotient (* (light-read) 1000) 4095). Never fails.

entries.name: backlight-set
entries.desc: Set LCD backlight brightness PWM (0-255); turns the automatic backlight off. Kept in config.ini [display] backlight.
entries.returns: Void. val is clamped to 0..255 (0 is dark); a non-integer is ignored. The firmware saves the level and auto_backlight = 0 to config.ini once changes stop for 3 s.

entries.name: backlight-get
entries.desc: Current LCD backlight brightness (0-255), set by backlight-set or by the automatic backlight.
entries.returns: An integer 0..255. Never fails.

entries.name: backlight-auto
entries.desc: Automatic backlight from the light sensor: #t while on; (backlight-auto #t) / #f turns it on / off. backlight-set turns it off. Kept in config.ini [display] auto_backlight.
entries.returns: #t or #f: the state after the call. Any value but #f turns it on, which moves the level half way to the target at once. Never fails.
entries.notes: Once a second the level moves half way to 60 + 195 x sqrt(light-read / 4095): about 70 in a dark room, 190 indoors, 255 in direct light.

entries.name: buzzer-tone
entries.desc: Play a tone.
entries.returns: #t at once: the tone (a 50 % PWM square wave) plays in the background for ms, or until buzzer-stop when ms is 0; a new tone replaces the one playing. An error when freq-hz is not 20..20000 or ms is negative. Absent on boards without a buzzer (the reference board).

entries.name: buzzer-stop
entries.desc: Silence the buzzer.
entries.returns: #t when a tone was playing, #f otherwise.

entries.name: backlight-offset
entries.desc: Get or set backlight brightness offset (-10 to 10) for automatic backlight calculation.
entries.returns: Current offset integer (-10 to 10).

entries.name: backlight-min
entries.desc: Get or set minimum backlight brightness level (0 to 255).
entries.returns: Current minimum backlight integer (0 to 255).

entries.name: backlight-max
entries.desc: Get or set maximum backlight brightness level (0 to 255).
entries.returns: Current maximum backlight integer (0 to 255).

entries.name: display-model
entries.desc: Panel model string.
entries.returns: String, "ILI9488-8BIT-PARALLEL-480x320" on every build.

entries.name: display-rotation
entries.desc: Panel rotation 0..3 (0 and 2 portrait 320x480, 1 and 3 landscape 480x320); returns the rotation.
entries.returns: Fixnum 0..3, the rotation after the call (r is taken modulo 4). Setting it re-initializes the screen in direct mode with the new size and clears it. A non-integer r is ignored.
entries.notes: The WASM simulator and the PC build keep a simulated rotation. Setting a rotation goes through `gui-init`, so the buffer mode becomes `direct` (see `gui-mode`) until the next boot; call `gui-invalidate` to have the app redrawn.

entries.name: display-dma-ram
entries.desc: Bytes of the LCD driver's DMA and staging buffers (0 without DMA).
entries.returns: Fixnum >= 0: the bytes on the board; always 0 in the WASM simulator and on the PC.

entries.name: gui-init
entries.desc: Re-initialize the screen as w x h pixels (default 320x480) in direct mode and clear it.
entries.returns: Void. Without two integers the default size is used; a size over 480x480 pixels keeps the current size.
entries.notes: Legacy: the firmware sets the screen up at boot from config.ini [display] (mode, band_lines, color_bits). `gui-init` always switches to direct mode; to change the size only use `gui-set-resolution`.

entries.name: gui-clear
entries.desc: Fill the current clip (the whole screen without one) with an RGB565 color (default dark slate 2179).
entries.returns: Void.
entries.notes: In `gui-render-proc` the clip is the span being redrawn, which the runtime has already cleared to 2179 (#0b1118). Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-flush
entries.desc: Mark the whole screen changed for the host canvas (simulator). The board sends pixels by itself.
entries.returns: Void.
entries.notes: Legacy. Apps redraw through `gui-invalidate` and `gui-render-proc`; in full mode `gui-flush-dirty` sends rows drawn outside a render at once.

entries.name: gui-pixel
entries.desc: Set one pixel to an RGB565 color; (gui-pixel x y) reads the stored color back.
entries.returns: Void when setting; with two arguments the RGB565 fixnum at x y (0 outside the screen or where no pixels are kept: band rows not being drawn, direct mode). Pixels outside the clip are skipped.
entries.notes: At color bits below 16 the read-back is the palette color the pixel was mapped to. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-line
entries.desc: Draw a one-pixel line between two points, both ends included.
entries.returns: Void; ignored unless all five arguments are integers.
entries.notes: Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-rect
entries.desc: Draw a rectangle, filled unless filled is #f (then a one-pixel outline).
entries.returns: Void; ignored unless x y w h color are integers or when w or h <= 0.
entries.notes: Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-round-rect
entries.sig: (gui-round-rect x y w h r color [filled])
entries.desc: Draw a rectangle with corners of radius r, filled unless filled is #f.
entries.returns: Void; ignored unless the first six arguments are integers. r is limited to half the width and height; r <= 0 draws a plain rectangle.
entries.notes: Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-circle
entries.desc: Draw a circle of radius r around cx cy, filled unless filled is #f.
entries.returns: Void; ignored unless the first four arguments are integers. r <= 0 draws the center pixel.
entries.notes: Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-text
entries.desc: Draw UTF-8 text with its top-left corner at x y in the current font; size 2.. draws the built-in 8x8 font scaled.
entries.returns: Void; ignored unless x y are integers, str a string and color an integer.
entries.notes: size 1 (default) is `gui-text-styled` with the current font (`gui-set-font`). Larger sizes scale the built-in 8x8 ASCII glyphs and 16x16 CJK glyphs by size; a "\n" starts a new line. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-set-font
entries.desc: Set the current font: 0 system 16 px, 1 clock 32 px (digits), 2..7 registered or loaded fonts.
entries.returns: Void. Any integer is kept; text in an id without a font uses the system font.
entries.notes: The current font is global (shared by every app until changed) and used by `gui-text`, `gui-text-width` and the text procedures whose font argument is left out.

entries.name: gui-get-font
entries.desc: The current font id (see gui-set-font).
entries.returns: Fixnum, the id last given to `gui-set-font` (0 at boot).

entries.name: gui-text-width
entries.desc: Width in pixels of str drawn in a font (default the current font).
entries.returns: Fixnum >= 0, the sum of the glyph advances; 0 when str is not a string.
entries.notes: Lay out text with it: right-align at xr with `(gui-text-styled (- xr (gui-text-width s f)) y s c f)`. A missing glyph counts as the width it is drawn with (the system font, or a box).

entries.name: gui-text-styled
entries.desc: Draw UTF-8 text with its top-left corner at x y in a font (default the current font).
entries.returns: Void; ignored unless x y are integers, str a string and color an integer.
entries.notes: Glyphs the font lacks come from the system font, then the built-in font; with none a box is drawn. "\n" starts a new line (font height + 2 lower). Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-text-box
entries.sig: (gui-text-box x y w h str color [font-id [halign [valign]]])
entries.desc: Draw one line of text aligned in a box and clipped to it. halign 0 left, 1 center, 2 right; valign 0 top, 1 middle, 2 bottom.
entries.returns: Void; ignored unless x y w h are integers, str a string and color an integer. font-id defaults to the current font, halign and valign to 0.
entries.notes: Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-text-scaled
entries.desc: Draw UTF-8 text in a font (default the current one) with every dot scale x scale (2..8): large text without a large font.
entries.returns: Void. scale 1 or less draws as gui-text-styled, more than 8 as 8. An error when x, y, color or scale is not an integer or str is not a string.
entries.example:
(gui-text-scaled 10 40 "阿莫西林" (gui-rgb 255 255 255) 2)   ; 16 px font -> 32 px
(gui-text-scaled 10 40 'name 0 2)  ; => error: expected
entries.notes: The glyphs of the font chain (the system font, its fallbacks) are enlarged: a dot set (an anti-aliased dot more than half covered) becomes a scale x scale square, so the edges are blocky but no font file is needed. Lines (\n) are (height + 2) x scale apart. Check it with (defined? 'gui-text-scaled) on older firmware. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-chart
entries.sig: (gui-chart x y w h ring start count lo hi color)
entries.desc: Line chart of count values of the vector ring from index start (wrapping), scaled from lo..hi to the box.
entries.returns: Void. An error when ring is not a vector or another argument is not an integer; nothing is drawn when count < 2 or hi <= lo.
entries.notes: Values are clamped to lo..hi; elements that are not integers count as lo. count is limited to the vector length and 320 points, h to 256. Points are spread evenly over w. A ring buffer of samples draws in order with start = the oldest index. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-image
entries.desc: Draw an image file at x y (its top-left corner): a baseline JPEG, or an animation (a MANI file of JPEG frames, which the photo album's web page makes from a GIF).
entries.returns: Void. frame: #t (the default) plays an animation by its frame delays, #f shows its first frame, a number that frame; speed: percent of the delays' pace, 10..1000 (100). path is in the app's folder like the fs- procedures. Errors: a file that cannot be opened or is not a baseline JPEG / MANI file (progressive JPEG, PNG and GIF need converting: the album's page does it in the browser).
entries.example: (gui-image 0 0 "photos/none.jpg")  ; => error: gui-image: cannot open the image file
entries.notes: One display-list command: a band decodes only the JPEG's MCU rows it covers (the decoder remembers where each one starts), so a full-screen photo needs no frame buffer; about 6 KB while an image is open. A playing animation redraws only its own box at its shortest frame delay, its clock starting when it appears. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: image-info
entries.desc: The size of an image file and its frames: (width height frames total-ms).
entries.returns: The list, or #f when the file is missing or not an image gui-image can draw. total-ms is an animation's length (0 for one frame).
entries.notes: Center an image: x = (320 - width) / 2. Opening an image reads only its headers.

entries.name: gui-bitmap
entries.sig: (gui-bitmap x y w h data scale fg [bg])
entries.desc: Draw a 1-bit bitmap of w x h dots, each dot scale x scale pixels: set dots in fg, clear ones in bg (left as they are without bg).
entries.returns: Void. data is a string of bytes: h rows of (w + 7) / 8 bytes each, the first dot of a byte its high bit (a row ends on a byte boundary). Errors: data shorter than that, w or h not 1..4096, scale not 1..255, another argument not an integer.
entries.example:
;; a 2 x 2 checker: rows #b10000000 and #b01000000, 10 px dots
(define checker (list->string (list (integer->char 128) (integer->char 64))))
(gui-bitmap 100 100 2 2 checker 10 (gui-rgb 255 255 255) 0)
(gui-pixel 105 105)  ; => 65535
(gui-pixel 115 105)  ; => 0
(gui-pixel 115 115)  ; => 65535
(gui-bitmap 0 0 16 2 checker 1 0)  ; => error: data has
entries.notes: One display-list command however many dots (the rows go to its string pool): a QR code or an icon costs what one rectangle does, where gui-rect per dot or per run used up the 512-command list. A band draws only its rows, each row's runs of set dots as single rectangles. Build data with list->string of (integer->char byte) values; it may hold 0 bytes. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-arc
entries.sig: (gui-arc cx cy r thickness start-deg sweep-deg color)
entries.desc: Draw a ring arc of outer radius r: 0 degrees is 3 o'clock, sweeping clockwise.
entries.returns: Void. An error when an argument is not an integer; nothing is drawn when r, thickness or sweep-deg <= 0. sweep-deg >= 360 draws the full ring.
entries.notes: A gauge: `(gui-arc cx cy r 8 135 (quotient (* 270 pct) 100) color)` over a dim full 270-degree track. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-push-clip
entries.desc: Save the current clip and clip drawing to the rectangle x y w h (no allocation).
entries.returns: Void. An error when an argument is not an integer or when pushes nest deeper than 8.
entries.notes: Pair every push with a `gui-pop-clip`. The stack is reset each time the runtime calls `gui-render-proc`. Inside a render the effective clip is also limited to the rows being redrawn.

entries.name: gui-pop-clip
entries.desc: Restore the clip saved by the matching gui-push-clip.
entries.returns: Void. An error when no clip is saved.

entries.name: gui-mode
entries.desc: Buffer mode: band (a few rows at a time), full (whole frame) or direct (no buffer).
entries.returns: Symbol band, full or direct. Set by config.ini [display] mode; full falls back to band, band to direct, when RAM is short.

entries.name: gui-color-bits
entries.desc: Bits per stored pixel: 16 (RGB565) or 8, 4, 2, 1 (palette indices); setting it redraws.
entries.returns: Fixnum, the bits after the call. An error when n is not 16, 8, 4, 2 or 1.
entries.notes: Fewer bits cost less buffer RAM (bits/16 of the RGB565 size); colors are mapped to the palette of the color scheme (`gui-color-scheme`). Changing it re-creates the buffer, clears the screen and queues a full redraw. Kept until the next boot (config.ini [display] color_bits sets the boot value).

entries.name: gui-color-scheme
entries.desc: Color scheme: color, gray, eink, green, amber, cyan, gameboy, invert (RGB negative) or custom.
entries.returns: Symbol, the scheme after the call. name is a symbol or string; older names (mono, e-ink, matrix, negative, ...) are accepted. An error for an unknown name.
entries.example:
(gui-color-scheme)          ; => color
(gui-color-scheme 'amber)   ; => amber
(gui-color-scheme "color")  ; => color
(gui-color-scheme 'sepia)   ; => error: unknown scheme
entries.notes: Ramp schemes (gray ... gameboy) map colors by brightness; at 16 bits they tint the screen with 64 levels. Setting a scheme queues a full redraw; it is kept until the next boot (config.ini [display] palette).

entries.name: gui-buffer-ram
entries.desc: Bytes held by the band or frame buffer (0 in direct mode).
entries.returns: Fixnum: width x rows x bits / 8 (the band rows in band mode, the screen in full mode).

entries.name: gui-card
entries.sig: (gui-card x y w h r bg-color border-color)
entries.desc: Rounded card: a filled background plus a one-pixel outline (border 0 or bg-color: none).
entries.returns: Void; ignored unless all seven arguments are integers. r 0 draws square corners.
entries.notes: Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-text-wrap
entries.sig: (gui-text-wrap x y w h str color [font [line-height]])
entries.desc: Draw text wrapped to width w, as many lines as fit in h; cut text ends with an ellipsis. Returns the lines drawn.
entries.returns: Fixnum, the number of lines drawn (at least 1 line is drawn when h is smaller than a line). An error when x y w h color are not integers or str is not a string.
entries.example:
(gui-text-wrap 10 10 100 200 "one two three four five six" 65535 0)  ; => 3
(gui-text-wrap 10 10 100 18 "one two three four five six" 65535 0)   ; => 1
entries.notes: Lines break at spaces, or between two characters when either is CJK (Latin words and numbers stay whole; closing punctuation never starts a line); "\n" forces a break. line-height defaults to the font height + 2. Use `gui-text-area` to scroll text that does not fit instead. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-text-fit
entries.desc: One line of text in a box w pixels wide; a longer line is cut with an ellipsis or scrolls as set by config.ini [text] marquee.
entries.returns: Void. An error when x y w color are not integers or str is not a string.
entries.example:
(gui-text-fit 10 10 120 "Short" 65535 0)
(gui-text-fit 10 30 120 "A headline much too long for its box" 65535 0)
entries.notes: The box is the font height + 2 tall. Modes (`gui-marquee`): none cuts the line with an ellipsis; pixel and char move it marquee_step pixels or characters marquee_fps times a second; page shows box-wide pieces in turn. Draw it from `gui-render-proc` every time: the runtime animates the box by redrawing only its rows (or its rectangle) without another `gui-invalidate`.

entries.name: gui-text-area
entries.sig: (gui-text-area x y w h str color [font [line-h]])
entries.desc: Text wrapped to a box; text taller than the box is cut with an ellipsis or scrolls as set by config.ini [text] wrap_marquee.
entries.returns: Void. An error when x y w h color are not integers or str is not a string.
entries.example: (gui-text-area 10 10 300 60 "A long news summary that needs several lines to fit in this box." 65535 0)
entries.notes: Wraps like `gui-text-wrap`; line-h defaults to the font height + 2. Modes (`gui-marquee 'wrap`): none cuts the text with an ellipsis; pixel rolls it up; line moves wrap_marquee_step lines at a time; page shows the next box-full; wrap_marquee_fps times a second. Draw it from `gui-render-proc`; the box animates by itself.

entries.name: gui-marquee
entries.desc: Marquee settings (mode fps step hold) of one-line text, or of wrapped text with 'wrap; arguments set them until the next boot.
entries.returns: List (mode fps step hold): mode a symbol, fps a number (0.1..25 refreshes a second), step a fixnum 1..64 (pixels, characters or lines), hold the seconds (0..10) the start stays. An error for a mode the kind does not take.
entries.example:
(define saved (gui-marquee))
(gui-marquee 'char 2 1 0.5)  ; => (char 2 1 0.5)
(gui-marquee 'wrap)          ; => (line 0.5 1 1)
(gui-marquee 'line)          ; => error: one-line text takes
(apply gui-marquee saved)
entries.notes: One-line text (`gui-text-fit`) takes none, pixel, char or page; wrapped text (`gui-text-area`) none, pixel, line or page. Arguments left out keep their values. The boot values come from config.ini [text] (marquee, marquee_fps, marquee_step, marquee_hold and the wrap_ ones); setting them queues a full redraw.

entries.name: gui-text-scroll
entries.sig: (gui-text-scroll x y w h str color [font [speed [direction]]])
entries.desc: Text longer than its box scrolls in a loop: direction 'left (marquee, default) or 'up (wrapped lines); speed in pixels per second (default 30).
entries.returns: Void. An error when x y w h color are not integers or str is not a string. speed is limited to 0..2000.
entries.example:
(define (render)
  (gui-text-scroll 10 10 200 20 "Breaking news: a very long headline scrolls" 65535 0 40))
(define gui-render-proc render)
(gui-invalidate)
entries.notes: Text that fits is drawn still. Draw it from `gui-render-proc` like other text; the offset comes from the frame clock and the runtime redraws only the box while it moves (up to 25 times a second), without running the render procedure again until the app calls `gui-invalidate`.

entries.name: gui-seg7
entries.sig: (gui-seg7 x y digit-w digit-h thickness str on off glow highlight)
entries.desc: Draw seven-segment digits (0-9, -, : and .); unlit segments in off, lit ones in on with optional glow and highlight colors.
entries.returns: Fixnum, the width drawn (as `gui-seg7-width`); 0 and nothing drawn when an argument has the wrong type.
entries.example:
(define on (gui-rgb 255 80 0))
(define off (gui-rgb 40 20 10))
(gui-seg7 10 10 30 56 6 "12:45" on off on on)  ; => 152
entries.notes: glow != on draws a halo around lit segments; highlight != on (thickness >= 5) a thin bright core. Pass on for both to draw plain segments. Characters other than the digits, "-", ":" and "." leave a blank digit. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-seg7-width
entries.desc: Width in pixels gui-seg7 draws for str.
entries.returns: Fixnum: digit-w per character, thickness + 2 per ":" or ".", plus thickness / 2 + 3 between characters; 0 for wrong arguments.

entries.name: gui-set-resolution
entries.desc: Change the logical screen size, keeping the buffer mode; the screen is cleared and redrawn.
entries.returns: Void. Ignored when w or h <= 0 or w x h is over 480x480 pixels.
entries.notes: It does not rotate the panel: use `display-rotation` for that. In band mode a wider screen gets fewer band rows so the band keeps its RAM.

entries.name: gui-set-clip
entries.desc: Clip drawing to a rectangle (limited to the screen).
entries.returns: Void; ignored unless all four arguments are integers. w or h <= 0 clips everything away.
entries.notes: Prefer `gui-push-clip` / `gui-pop-clip`, which restore the caller's clip.

entries.name: gui-reset-clip
entries.desc: Remove the clip rectangle: drawing reaches the whole screen again.
entries.returns: Void.

entries.name: gui-get-clip
entries.desc: Current clip rectangle as (x y w h).
entries.returns: List of four fixnums; (0 0 width height) without a clip.

entries.name: gui-dirty-rect
entries.desc: Bounding box of the screen area changed since the host canvas last took it, as (x y w h).
entries.returns: List of four fixnums; (0 0 0 0) when nothing changed.
entries.notes: For hosts that paint a canvas (the WASM simulator); apps do not need it.

entries.name: gui-mark-dirty
entries.desc: Mark a rectangle as changed for the host canvas.
entries.returns: Void; ignored unless all four arguments are integers.
entries.notes: It does not redraw anything: to have the app redraw use `gui-invalidate`.

entries.name: gui-dirty-rect-count
entries.desc: Number of dirty rectangles after merging (at most 8).
entries.returns: Fixnum 0..8.

entries.name: gui-dirty-rects
entries.desc: Dirty rectangles after merging into 32-pixel tiles, as a list of (x y w h).
entries.returns: List of up to 8 lists (x y w h), top to bottom; () when nothing changed.

entries.name: gui-flush-dirty
entries.desc: Full mode: send the rows drawn outside a render to the panel now.
entries.returns: Void. On the PC build it also clears the dirty rectangles.
entries.notes: The runtime sends such rows at its next display service anyway; call it when the app draws outside `gui-render-proc` and must show the result before a long computation. Other modes: no effect on the panel.

entries.name: gui-render-bands
entries.desc: Call proc once per slice of band-h rows, drawing clipped to the slice: (lambda (i y h) ...) or (lambda (i) ...).
entries.returns: #t; void when band-h is not an integer (nothing is called).
entries.example:
(define n 0)
(gui-render-bands 160 (lambda (i y h) (set! n (+ n 1))))  ; => #t
n  ; => 3
entries.notes: Legacy immediate rendering: in band mode each slice is sent to the panel after proc returns, in full mode the frame after the last slice. band-h is limited to the band rows in band mode. Called from `gui-render-proc` it cannot be recorded, so the render procedure then runs once per band; prefer `gui-render-proc` with `gui-visible?`.

entries.name: gui-create-buffer
entries.desc: Create an offscreen RGB565 buffer of w x h pixels; returns its id.
entries.returns: Fixnum id 1..15; -1 when w or h is not a positive integer, memory is short or all 15 buffers are in use.
entries.notes: The buffer holds w x h x 2 bytes of C heap (not the VM heap) until `gui-destroy-buffer`; it starts black.

entries.name: gui-destroy-buffer
entries.desc: Free an offscreen buffer (drawing returns to the screen if it was the target).
entries.returns: Void; an unknown id is ignored.

entries.name: gui-set-target
entries.desc: Draw into offscreen buffer id (0 = the screen); the clip becomes the whole target.
entries.returns: Void; an unknown id is ignored.
entries.notes: Ignored while `gui-render-proc` is being recorded (band mode then runs the render procedure once per band). Prepare buffers outside the render procedure.

entries.name: gui-reset-target
entries.desc: Draw to the screen again (same as (gui-set-target 0)).
entries.returns: Void.

entries.name: gui-blit-buffer
entries.desc: Copy an offscreen buffer to the current target at x y (clipped).
entries.returns: Void; an unknown id is ignored.
entries.notes: Cannot be recorded: called from `gui-render-proc` in band mode, the render procedure runs once per band. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

entries.name: gui-framebuffer-enable
entries.desc: Switch to full mode (true) or direct mode (#f); returns whether full mode is on.
entries.returns: #t in full mode after the call, else #f (full mode needs RAM for the frame: without it the mode becomes band).
entries.notes: Switching re-creates the buffer, clears the screen and queues a full redraw.

entries.name: gui-framebuffer-enabled?
entries.desc: True in full (frame buffer) mode.
entries.returns: #t in full mode, #f in band or direct mode.

entries.name: gui-framebuffer-ram
entries.desc: Bytes held by the band or frame buffer (same as gui-buffer-ram).
entries.returns: Fixnum, 0 in direct mode.

entries.name: gui-color-depth
entries.desc: Legacy gui-color-bits: bits per stored pixel; a value other than 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 is ignored.
entries.returns: Fixnum, the bits per pixel after the call. Never an error.

entries.name: gui-color-format
entries.desc: Panel bus format: rgb565 or rgb666 (config.ini [display] color_format).
entries.returns: Symbol rgb565 or rgb666.

entries.name: gui-mono-colors
entries.desc: Two-color custom palette: sets entries 0 = bg and 1 = fg and the custom scheme; returns (fg bg).
entries.returns: List (fg bg) of RGB565 fixnums: the ones set, or the brightest and darkest colors of the current palette (white and 2179 at 16 bits).
entries.notes: Meant for 1-bit color (`gui-color-bits` 1).

entries.name: gui-palette-set!
entries.desc: Set palette entry 0..255 and switch to the custom scheme (starting from the current palette).
entries.returns: Void; ignored when an argument is not an integer or index is outside 0..255.
entries.notes: Only the first 2^bits entries are used (`gui-color-bits`). Queues a full redraw.

entries.name: gui-palette-get
entries.desc: RGB565 color of a palette entry of the current scheme.
entries.returns: Fixnum; 0 for an index the palette does not have (at 16 bits the color scheme has no palette) or a non-integer index.

entries.name: gui-palette-preset
entries.desc: Legacy gui-color-scheme: set a scheme by name; #f for an unknown name.
entries.returns: #t when name (symbol or string) is a known scheme, else #f (no error).

entries.name: gui-band-lines
entries.desc: Rows per band in band mode (config.ini [display] band_lines).
entries.returns: Fixnum: the band rows in band mode; in the other modes the configured value.

entries.name: gui-rgb
entries.desc: RGB565 color of 8-bit red, green and blue (0..255).
entries.returns: Fixnum 0..65535: r and b keep 5 bits, g 6. Components wrap modulo 256; 0 unless all three are integers.

entries.name: gui-width
entries.desc: Screen width in pixels (320 in portrait, 480 in landscape).
entries.returns: Fixnum.

entries.name: gui-height
entries.desc: Screen height in pixels (480 in portrait, 320 in landscape).
entries.returns: Fixnum.

entries.name: gui-touch-poll
entries.desc: The touch point as (x . y) while the screen is touched, else #f.
entries.returns: Pair of fixnums or #f. Only the WASM simulator reports touches (a click on its canvas); the board has no touch panel: always #f.

entries.name: gui-touch-down?
entries.desc: True while the screen is touched.
entries.returns: #t or #f (always #f on the board, see `gui-touch-poll`).

entries.name: gui-invalidate
entries.desc: Queue rows y..y+h-1 (the whole screen without arguments) to be redrawn by gui-render-proc.
entries.returns: Void. Only y and h count (whole rows are redrawn); (gui-invalidate y h) is also accepted.
entries.notes: The redraw happens after the current event, at the next display service: the runtime clears the queued rows to 2179 and calls `gui-render-proc` (no arguments) with drawing clipped to them. Queue only the rows that changed. Calls made while the render procedure runs are ignored.

entries.name: gui-visible?
entries.desc: Whether rows y..y+h-1 meet the area being drawn; skip the drawing of a section when #f.
entries.returns: #t or #f; #t when the arguments are not two integers.
entries.notes: Compares with the current clip: in `gui-render-proc` the rows being redrawn. In band mode the render procedure runs once for the whole span, so it skips sections outside what `gui-invalidate` queued.

entries.name: font-load
entries.desc: Load an MFNT font file (tools/make_font.py) into slot 2..7. Small files go to RAM; large ones (or 'stream) are read glyph by glyph. An app loads only files of its own folder.
entries.returns: #t. An error when id is not 2..7, path is not a string, or the file cannot be read or is not a valid MFNT font.
entries.notes: Needs an MFNT file on the board (or the simulator's file system). Files up to 24 KB are read into RAM on the board; larger ones stay on flash behind a glyph cache. The slot then holds only that font; loading queues a full redraw.

entries.name: font-register!
entries.desc: Use MFNT font bytes for slot 2..7, e.g. (include-bytes "x.mfnt"); a Code ROM literal is read in place, a heap string copied.
entries.returns: #t when the slot holds a font afterwards. An error when id is not 2..7, bytes is not a string or not a valid MFNT font.
entries.notes: The font's name (stored in it) also brings the other sources of config.ini [fonts] font_order (font ROM, files) to fill glyphs it lacks. Queues a full redraw.

entries.name: font-unload
entries.desc: Empty font slot 2..7; its text falls back to the system font.
entries.returns: Void. An error when id is not 2..7.

entries.name: font-info
entries.desc: (name height glyphs source bytes) of a font slot; #f for an empty slot.
entries.returns: List: name string, height in pixels, glyph count, source symbol (builtin, rom, ram, file or fontrom: the first source of the chain) and the bytes it holds (0 for builtin). #f for an empty slot or a non-integer id.
entries.notes: Slots 0 and 1 report builtin unless config.ini [fonts] font_override replaces them.

entries.name: font-config
entries.desc: Font sources and replacements (config.ini [fonts] font_order, font_override); with arguments set them and resolve every font again.
entries.returns: List (sources overrides): the source symbols in order and a list of ("name" . "replacement") pairs. An error for an unknown source, a source listed twice, or an override not written name:replacement.
entries.example:
(font-config)  ; => ((app fontrom spiffs) ())
(font-config "fontrom, app" "system_16:simsun-16")  ; => ((fontrom app) (("system_16" . "simsun-16")))
(font-config "app, fontrom, spiffs" "")  ; => ((app fontrom spiffs) ())
(font-config "web")  ; => error: font_order
entries.notes: Sources: app (fonts the app carries), fontrom (the system font ROM), spiffs (/spiffs/fonts/<name>.mfnt). An override puts the sources of the replacement first; system_16 (or 0) and clock_32 (or 1) name the built-in fonts. Kept until the next boot; queues a full redraw.

entries.name: font-server
entries.desc: The font server: glyphs the fonts lack (or, with font_server_first, all system-font text) fetched on demand and kept on the board.
entries.returns: An alist: (on . #t/#f), (url . "..."), (first . #t/#f), (face . "simsun") and (size . 16) asked for, (state . s) with s one of off, idle, queued, fetching, waiting (after a failure, retried in 5 s, after 3 failures every 60 s), (pending . n) code points waiting, (received . n) and (absent . n) glyphs since boot (absent: no font of the server has it), (requests . n), (error . "") the last failure. Never an error.
entries.notes: config.ini [fonts]: font_server (URL, default http://124.222.231.186:8090, a service of its own: minischeme-proxy font_server.py, no password, no app server needed), font_server_on (0: never ask), font_server_first (1: the server's face first for system-font text; the board's glyphs stand in until the server's arrive), font_server_face (the face asked for; empty: the system font's, simsun). The settings page applies them at once. Glyphs are kept in /spiffs/fonts/net-<face>-<size>.mgh (512 slots, 2048 with font_server_first) and a small RAM cache (about 1 KB, 4.6 KB with font_server_first); a character drawn before its glyph arrived is redrawn when it does. Text keeps working without a network: what no font has is drawn as a box. Emoji and other code points above U+FFFF come only from the font server; variation selectors and joiners (U+FE0F, U+200D) are drawn as nothing.

entries.name: font-server-clear
entries.desc: Drops the glyphs downloaded from the font server (they are asked for again when drawn).
entries.returns: #t. Queues a full redraw.
entries.notes: The board drops them by itself when the server's fonts change (the server sends an identity with every reply).

entries.name: font-sources
entries.desc: The chain searched for each glyph of slot id, in order, as ((source name height glyphs bits) ...).
entries.returns: List of lists: source symbol (rom, ram, file, fontrom), name, height, glyph count and bits per pixel (1, 2 or 4). () for an empty slot or a built-in font.
entries.notes: A glyph no source has comes from the system font.

entries.name: font-use
entries.desc: Font slot 2..7 for this app: face-size from the app's embedded subset, the font ROM or a file (config.ini [fonts] font_order). #f when no source has it.
entries.returns: #t when slot id holds a font afterwards (also when it already held one: the slot is not changed), else #f and its text uses the system font. An error when id is not 2..7 or face is not a string.
entries.example:
(define f (if (font-use 3 "simhei" 24) 3 0))
f  ; => 0
(font-use 1 "simhei" 24)  ; => error: font id must be 2..7
entries.notes: tools/build_apps.py embeds a subset of the face (the characters of the app's strings) unless the form ends with 'system or the build uses --system-fonts. At run time the name <face>-<size> is looked up in the sources of font_order (app, fontrom, spiffs): the font the app carries, the system font ROM, /spiffs/fonts/<face>-<size>.mfnt. A face with a '/' is a file path. Queues a full redraw when it fills the slot.

entries.name: fontrom-list
entries.desc: Fonts in the system font ROM (flash partition, read in place) as ((name height glyphs bytes) ...).
entries.returns: List of lists: name string, height in pixels, glyph count, size in bytes; () without a font ROM partition.
entries.notes: On a board with a font ROM it gives e.g. (("msyh-16" 16 7000 250000) ...). `font-use` finds the fonts by name <face>-<size>.

entries.name: fontrom-info
entries.desc: (used capacity count) of the system font ROM: bytes used, partition bytes, fonts.
entries.returns: List of three fixnums; #f when the firmware has no fontrom partition (the WASM simulator and the PC build have none).

entries.name: fontrom-add
entries.desc: Copy an MFNT font file into the system font ROM (name defaults to the one in the font; the same name replaces it). Not for apps: only the system settings and the REPL may (an app gets an error).
entries.returns: String, the name stored. An error when path or name is not a string, there is no font ROM partition, or the file cannot be read, is not a font or does not fit.
entries.notes: On the board: `(fontrom-add "/spiffs/fonts/simhei-24.mfnt")` => "simhei-24". Slots using font ROM fonts are resolved again; queues a full redraw.

entries.name: fontrom-remove
entries.desc: Remove a font from the system font ROM; later fonts move down. Not for apps: only the system settings and the REPL may (an app gets an error).
entries.returns: #t when removed, #f when there is no such font (or no font ROM). An error when name is not a string or the flash write fails.

entries.name: lunar-date
entries.desc: The Chinese lunar date of a Gregorian date as (month day leap?).
entries.returns: List: lunar month 1..12, day 1..30, #t in a leap month. #f for dates before 1900-01-31 or after 2100, months outside 1..12, days outside 1..31 or non-integer arguments.
entries.notes: The day is not checked against the month: 2024-02-30 counts as 2024-03-01.

entries.name: lunar-date-string
entries.desc: The lunar date as Chinese display text for the screen.
entries.returns: String "农历" + optional "闰" (leap) + month + "月" + day; #f where `lunar-date` gives #f.
entries.example:
(lunar-date-string 2024 2 10)  ; => "农历正月初一"
(lunar-date-string 2023 3 22)  ; => "农历闰二月初一"

entries.name: theme-css
entries.desc: The system color scheme file /spiffs/theme.css as a string; any app may read it (gui.scm resolves color aliases with it).
entries.returns: A string of the file (binary-safe), or #f when there is none or it is over 16 KB. Never fails. Apps write only their own folder: the file is written by the device page or the system settings.
entries.notes: The format is CSS-like: blocks named after a scheme (day, night, or a name of your own; * for every scheme) holding alias: value; pairs, a value being #rgb, #rrggbb, rgb(r, g, b) or another alias; /* comments */. An app may keep its own theme.css in its folder (read with fs-read), which wins over this file. The cascade, the built-in schemes and the day/night switch are in docs/applib.md of minischeme-apps.

entries.name: wifi-connect
entries.desc: Join a WiFi network as a station. The connection completes in the background and is retried automatically when it drops. Not for apps: only the system settings and the REPL may (an app gets an error).
entries.returns: #t when the attempt has started (poll `(wifi-connected?)` for the link); #f when ssid is empty, an argument is not a string or the WiFi driver failed to start. Never an error. The board joins the network of config.ini at boot by itself.

entries.name: wifi-ap
entries.desc: Start a WiFi access point beside the station (address 192.168.4.1); a password under 8 characters makes it open. Not for apps: only the system settings and the REPL may (an app gets an error).
entries.returns: #t when the access point is up; #f when ssid is empty, an argument is not a string or the driver refused. Never an error. The station keeps its connection.

entries.name: wifi-connected?
entries.desc: Whether the station is connected and has an IP address.
entries.returns: #t or #f. Never an error.

entries.name: wifi-disconnect
entries.desc: Disconnect the station and stop the automatic reconnect; with #t the link drops and reconnects at once. Not for apps: only the system settings and the REPL may (an app gets an error).
entries.returns: Void. Never an error. The reconnect? argument is honored by the firmware only; the simulator and the PC mocks just disconnect.

entries.name: wifi-ip
entries.desc: The station IP address as a dotted string.
entries.returns: A string such as "192.168.1.42"; "0.0.0.0" while not connected. Never an error.

entries.name: wifi-rssi
entries.desc: Signal strength of the connected network in dBm.
entries.returns: A negative integer such as -52 (dBm; closer to 0 is stronger); 0 while not connected. Never an error.

entries.name: wifi-ssid
entries.desc: The SSID of the connected network.
entries.returns: A string; "" while not connected. Never an error.

entries.name: json-feed-start
entries.desc: Poll a JSON URL in the background; keep objects whose captured key matches a selector (key-index 'equal|'prefix string). A new call replaces the feed and fetches at once. An https:// URL goes through the protocol converter (config.ini [app] https_proxy, else proxy) as <it>/fetch?url=...; the board's own address is refused.
entries.returns: #t once the feed is configured. Errors: "json-feed-start: expected url interval-ms keys selectors ..." (url not a string, interval-ms not an integer), "keys must be strings", "selector must be (key-index 'equal|'prefix string)" (key-index not a key, another mode), "out of memory". interval-ms under 200 counts as 200. pool-bytes (value text per document), value-len (bytes per value) and depth (nesting levels captured) are limits the app chooses: omitted, 0 or #f means none (since 1.2.0; before, they were clamped to 256..16384, 16..256 and 1..8 with defaults 1536, 40 and 8). Any number of keys and selectors, of any length.
entries.notes:
**Model.** One feed per device. On the board a background task fetches the URL
with an HTTP GET (redirects are not followed; timeout: interval-ms clamped to
3..15 s) and streams the response through a JSON scanner: the document itself
is never held in RAM. A failed fetch is retried within 5 s, a good one after
interval-ms (at least 200 ms). The WASM simulator fetches for the feed through
the page (minischeme-webrepl server.py serves the app proxy's `/app/` routes); the PC REPL
and the test VM have no fetcher, so their feed never gets a document. A new
`json-feed-start` replaces the whole configuration and the board fetches the
new URL at once (an app switching pages); documents of an older configuration
are never shown: `json-feed-seq` returns 0 until the first document of the new
one is taken.

**Capture.** `keys` names any number of keys of any length; key k is the
k-th name. Every JSON object nested at most `depth` objects deep (the
top-level object is depth 1; arrays do not count; no depth: every level) is
scanned for those keys; their scalar values are captured as text: strings
unescaped (UTF-8), numbers, `true`, `false` and `null` as written. With a
value-len, at most that many bytes of a value are kept (cut at a UTF-8
character boundary); without one, values are kept whole. Objects and arrays
are not values.

**Selection.** A selector is `(key-index mode string [keep-key ...])`, mode
`'equal` or `'prefix`; there may be any number of them. A captured object
becomes a row when the value of key key-index equals (or starts with) the
string; the first matching selector wins and `(json-feed-selector i)` tells
which. The optional keep-keys limit the values stored for that row (all
captured keys when omitted): `(0 equal "error" 1)` keeps only key 1.
`(0 prefix "")` keeps every object that has key 0. A document keeps any
number of rows; with a pool-bytes, at most that much value text. When rows or
text do not fit (pool-bytes, or memory: on the board the feed leaves 16 KB of
heap free for the system) the status reports `truncated` #t. A document in
which no object had a captured key counts as a failed fetch ("no matching JSON
objects in the response").

**Reading.** `(json-feed-seq)` takes the newest complete document; `count`,
`field`, `ints` and `selector` then read that document, unchanged until a later
`json-feed-seq` takes the next one. Call it once per tick and redraw when the
number changes. `field` and `ints` take a key's index or (since 1.2.0) its name.

**With the app proxy.** The app proxy (minischeme-proxy) turns web APIs into flat documents
`{"items":[{"t":type,"a":..,"b":..,"c":..,"d":..,"e":..}]}` with series as
comma-separated integers; an app may name more keys (applib `app-keys!`).
apps/lib/applib.scm starts the feed with
`(json-feed-start url interval APP-KEYS '((0 prefix "")) 0 0 2)` and reads
every row with `json-feed-field` (`json-feed-ints` for series).

**Memory.** Nothing has a fixed size: the scanner's buffers (one per nesting
level), two snapshots (the one being filled and the one being read) and the
selectors are allocated as a feed needs them and kept for the next document.
`(json-feed-status)` reports the bytes held (`memory`). Until 1.2.0 a feed had
at most 6 keys of 23 bytes, 40 selectors, 64 rows, 16 KB of text, values of
255 bytes, 8 levels and a 255-byte URL.

entries.name: json-feed-ints
entries.desc: Integers of a comma-separated value of row i, key k: "12,-3,7" => (12 -3 7), or #f.
entries.returns: A list of integers (any number; a part without digits is skipped, "2.5" counts as 2); () for an empty value; #f when row i or its key k does not exist in the taken document. k is an index or (since 1.2.0) a key name. Never an error.
entries.example:
;; a proxy row {"t":"temp","a":"Mon","b":"12,15,9,-3"} gives (12 15 9 -3)
(define (series i) (or (json-feed-ints i 2) '()))
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/weather?loc=auto" 600000
                 '("t" "a" "b") '((0 prefix "")))
(series 0)   ; => ()

entries.name: json-feed-stop
entries.desc: Stop polling: the fetcher idles. The document already taken stays readable.
entries.returns: Void. Never an error.

entries.name: json-feed-seq
entries.desc: Take the newest complete document, if one arrived; returns its number (0 = none yet).
entries.returns: An integer: the number of the document now readable (one higher per document taken); 0 while the current feed (since the last json-feed-start) has no document. Never an error.
entries.example:
(define last-seq 0)
(define (feed-poll! redraw)
  (let ((seq (json-feed-seq)))
    (if (and (> seq 0) (not (= seq last-seq)))
        (begin (set! last-seq seq) (redraw)))))
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/ping" 60000 '("t") '((0 prefix "")))
(json-feed-seq)   ; => 0

entries.name: json-feed-count
entries.desc: Rows (selected objects) of the taken document.
entries.returns: An integer, 0 or more; 0 before the current feed has a document. Never an error.
entries.example:
(define (feed-titles)
  (let loop ((i (- (json-feed-count) 1)) (acc '()))
    (if (< i 0) acc (loop (- i 1) (cons (json-feed-field i 1) acc)))))
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/news?cat=finance" 300000
                 '("t" "a") '((0 equal "news")))
(feed-titles)   ; => ()

entries.name: json-feed-selector
entries.desc: Index of the selector that row i matched.
entries.returns: An integer (0 for the first selector of json-feed-start); #f when row i does not exist in the taken document. Never an error.

entries.name: json-feed-field
entries.desc: Captured value of key k (an index into keys, or since 1.2.0 a key name) for row i, as a string, or #f.
entries.returns: A string: the value as text (strings unescaped, numbers and true/false/null as written), whole or at most value-len bytes; #f when row i does not exist, the object lacked key k (or k names no key), or the selector did not keep it. Never an error.
entries.example:
;; row {"t":"news","a":"Markets rally","b":"10:42"}: (json-feed-field i 1) => "Markets rally"
(define (field-or i k default) (or (json-feed-field i k) default))
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/news?cat=finance" 300000
                 '("t" "a" "b") '((0 equal "news")))
(field-or 0 1 "(loading)")   ; => "(loading)"
;; by name, the same key as index 1:
(json-feed-field 0 "a")      ; => #f

entries.name: json-feed-url
entries.desc: The URL being polled, or #f.
entries.returns: A string: the URL of the last json-feed-start; #f before any or after json-feed-stop. Never an error.

entries.name: json-feed-status
entries.desc: Feed state as an alist: state, error, fetches, failures, bytes, fetch-ms, age-ms, objects, truncated, memory.
entries.returns: An alist in this order: (state . idle|connecting|ok|error), (error . message of the last failed fetch, "" after a good one: "WiFi not connected", "cannot connect", "HTTP status 404", "read error after N bytes", "no matching JSON objects in the response"), (fetches . n) and (failures . n) since boot, (bytes . size of the last response), (fetch-ms . duration of the last fetch, board only, else 0), (age-ms . ms since the last good document, -1 if none), (objects . objects with a captured key in the taken document), (truncated . #t when rows or value text did not fit: pool-bytes, value-len or memory), (memory . bytes the feed holds, since 1.2.0). Never an error.

entries.name: json-feed-dump
entries.desc: Every object of a document with captured keys, values joined by TAB, one per line.
entries.returns: A string (as long as the document needs, memory permitting): one line per object that had any captured key, selected or not, its values in key order joined by TAB. On the board it waits up to 6 s for the next fetched document; the simulator lists the last one. #f when no document came (or no feed was started). Never an error.
entries.example:
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/news?cat=finance" 300000
                 '("t" "a") '((0 equal "news")))
(display (or (json-feed-dump) "no document\n"))
;; prints one line per object, e.g. news<TAB>Markets rally

entries.name: http-get
entries.desc: Fetch a URL and wait for the response: (status . body).
entries.returns: A pair (status . body): status the HTTP status as an integer (any status, 404 too, is a result; redirects are not followed), body the response body as a string of its bytes. headers: an alist of (name . value) strings. Blocks the app until the response is complete, at most 10 s. Errors: "http-get: WiFi not connected", "http-get: cannot connect", "http-get: timeout", "http-get: response larger than 16384 bytes", a url not http:// or https://.

entries.name: http-post
entries.desc: Post a string body and wait for the response: (status . body).
entries.returns: A pair (status . body) as http-get. content-type defaults to "application/json". Blocks the app until the response is complete, at most 10 s. Errors as http-get, prefixed "http-post:".

entries.name: mqtt-connect
entries.desc: Connect to a broker (mqtt:// or mqtts://, user:password@ allowed); reconnects by itself later.
entries.returns: #t once the broker accepted the connection (waits at most 10 s). client-id defaults to "minischeme-" and the last 6 hex digits of the MAC. A second call replaces the connection. After a drop the client reconnects and subscribes again by itself. Errors: "mqtt-connect: WiFi not connected", "cannot connect", "timeout", "refused by the broker (code N)".

entries.name: mqtt-disconnect
entries.desc: Close the connection; forget subscriptions and queued messages.
entries.returns: Void; also when not connected. Never an error.

entries.name: mqtt-publish
entries.desc: Publish a string payload to a topic.
entries.returns: #t once the message is handed to the client (QoS 1 and 2 are delivered with retries in the background). qos 0, 1 or 2 (default 0); retain? default #f. Errors: "mqtt-publish: not connected", "qos must be 0, 1 or 2", a topic or payload not a string.

entries.name: mqtt-subscribe
entries.desc: Subscribe to a topic filter (+ and # wildcards); messages queue for mqtt-poll.
entries.returns: #t once the broker acknowledged the subscription. qos 0, 1 or 2 (default 0). Subscriptions are renewed after a reconnect. Errors: "mqtt-subscribe: not connected", "qos must be 0, 1 or 2", "refused by the broker".

entries.name: mqtt-poll
entries.desc: The next message received: (topic . payload), or #f.
entries.returns: A pair of strings (topic . payload), oldest first; #f when the queue is empty or not connected. The queue keeps 16 messages; when full the oldest is dropped. Never an error.

entries.name: fs-read
entries.desc: Read a whole file as a string.
entries.returns: A string of the file's bytes (binary-safe: NUL bytes included); #f when the file cannot be opened (missing) or path is not a string. Never an error.
entries.notes:
Files of the board's file system live under `/spiffs/` (LittleFS). An app may
touch only its own folder (`/spiffs/apps/<id>/`, or `/spiffs/user/<id>/` for an
uploaded app): a relative path such as `"notes.txt"` is in that folder, an
absolute one must be; its image there (app.msbc) is read-only and the folder
holds at most config.ini [system] app_storage_kb (256 KB, the image included).
Anything else is an error. The system settings and code from the REPL are not
limited (relative paths are then under `/spiffs`). The WASM simulator keeps its
files in the page and accepts only paths under `/spiffs/` (at most 63 bytes, no
`..`); the PC REPL and the test VM keep them in memory. Strings are byte
strings, so any UTF-8 text round-trips.

entries.name: fs-write
entries.desc: Create or replace a file with the bytes of a string.
entries.returns: #t when the whole string was written; #f when the file cannot be created (missing directory, file system full, in the simulator a path outside /spiffs/) or an argument is not a string. Never an error.

entries.name: fs-exists?
entries.desc: Whether a file exists (paths under /spiffs/).
entries.returns: #t when the file exists and can be opened; #f otherwise or when path is not a string. Never an error.

entries.name: fs-remove
entries.desc: Delete a file.
entries.returns: #t when the file was deleted; #f when it does not exist, cannot be deleted or path is not a string. Never an error.

entries.name: fs-info
entries.desc: Total and used bytes of the file system: (total used).
entries.returns: A list of two integers (total used) in bytes. Never an error.
entries.example:
(let* ((info (fs-info)) (free (- (car info) (cadr info))))
  (string-append (number->string (quotient free 1024)) " KB free"))
; e.g. "1210 KB free"

entries.name: fs-list
entries.desc: Files directly in a directory with their sizes: (("name" . bytes) ...).
entries.returns: A list of pairs (name . size) for the regular files directly in dir (subdirectories are left out; names without the directory); () when dir does not exist or is not /spiffs or under /spiffs/. Error "fs-list: expected a directory path" when dir is missing or not a string.

entries.name: fs-download
entries.desc: Download a file from the network into the app's folder, in the background (an image for gui-image, for example); one download at a time. on-done, if given, is called as (on-done ok path) when it ends.
entries.returns: #t when the download is queued; #f while another download is still running (try again after it, see fs-download-status). Errors: url not http:// or https://, path outside the app's folder (the same rule as fs-write), the app's storage full, on-done not a procedure.
entries.example:
;; a picture from the app server into the app's folder, then drawn
(define (cover-done ok path)        ; ok: #t when the file is complete
  (if ok (gui-invalidate 0 0 320 480)))   ; render then draws (gui-image x y "cache/7.jpg")
(fs-download (app-url "/app/myapp/pic?id=7") "cache/7.jpg" cover-done)   ; => #t
entries.notes: The board fetches over plain HTTP like the JSON feed (the device headers go to configured servers; an https:// URL goes through the protocol converter), after the feed's current request. The body is written to path.part and replaces path only when complete: a failed download leaves the old file. At most 256 KB, and no more than the app's storage quota has left. gui-image draws baseline JPEG only: let the app server convert pictures (size and format) before the board downloads them. In the WebREPL simulator the page fetches the file through server.py. on-done (since 1.12.0) is called by the main loop, between two app steps, as soon as the download is done (ok #t) or failed (ok #f; the message is in fs-download-status); it may start the next download at once. It is called once, and not at all when another app runs by then. Firmware before 1.12 ignores on-done: an app that also runs there checks fs-download-status from app-tick-proc as well.

entries.name: fs-download-status
entries.desc: The state of the last fs-download: (state path bytes error seq) as an alist.
entries.returns: An alist: (state . s) with s one of idle, queued, running, done, error; (path . "the path given"); (bytes . n) written when done; (error . "message") when it failed ("" otherwise); (seq . k), which grows by one each time a download ends (done or error), so a change means a new outcome. Never an error.

entries.name: fs-rename
entries.desc: Rename or move a file; an existing target is not replaced.
entries.returns: #t when renamed; #f when from does not exist, to already exists or the file system refuses. Error "fs-rename: expected two path strings" when an argument is not a string.

entries.name: fs-append
entries.desc: Append the bytes of a string to a file, creating it when missing.
entries.returns: #t when all of data was appended; #f when the file cannot be opened or written (file system full). Error "fs-append: expected a path and a string" when an argument is not a string.

entries.name: fs-size
entries.desc: Size of a file in bytes, or #f.
entries.returns: An integer (bytes); #f when the file does not exist. Error "fs-size: expected a path string" when path is not a string.

entries.name: kv-get
entries.desc: A value stored with kv-set! (a string), or default. Each app has its own keys.
entries.returns: The stored string; default (#f when omitted) when the key is not stored. key: a string or symbol of 1..15 bytes, else error "kv-get: key must be 1..15 bytes". Keys belong to the running app (its id is the namespace).

entries.name: kv-set!
entries.desc: Store a string under a key, kept across restarts (NVS on the board).
entries.returns: #t once the value is committed to flash. Errors: "kv-set!: key must be 1..15 bytes", "value must be a string of at most 4000 bytes", "store full".

entries.name: kv-remove
entries.desc: Delete a key of the running app.
entries.returns: #t when the key was removed; #f when it was not stored. Error "kv-remove: key must be 1..15 bytes".

entries.name: kv-keys
entries.desc: The keys stored by the running app.
entries.returns: A list of key strings in no particular order; () when none. Never an error.

entries.name: cfasl-compress
entries.desc: Compress a byte string with LZSS (4 KB window, matches of 3..18 bytes).
entries.returns: The compressed bytes as a string (keep the original length: cfasl-decompress needs it); () when byte-str is empty or not a string. Incompressible data can grow to twice its size (bytes >= 128 cost two bytes each). Never an error.

entries.name: cfasl-decompress
entries.desc: Decompress LZSS bytes made by cfasl-compress; uncomp-size is the original length.
entries.returns: A string of exactly uncomp-size bytes (a smaller uncomp-size gives the first bytes); () when the data is corrupt or yields fewer bytes, or an argument has the wrong type. Never an error.
entries.example:
(define s "ABCDEF1234567890ABCDEF1234567890")
(define c (cfasl-compress s))
(equal? (cfasl-decompress c (string-length s)) s)   ; => #t
(cfasl-decompress c 6)     ; => "ABCDEF"
(cfasl-decompress c 100)   ; => ()

entries.name: cfasl-make-stub
entries.sig: (cfasl-make-stub comp-code code-bytes nparams max-stack variadic? inner-lambdas? constants)
entries.desc: Make a demand-paged procedure stub from compressed bytecode; cfasl-call decompresses and runs it.
entries.returns: The stub, a vector #(cfasl-stub comp-code code-bytes nparams max-stack variadic? inner-lambdas? constants); () when fewer than 7 arguments are given, comp-code is not a non-empty string or code-bytes (the uncompressed length) is not an integer. The bytecode is not checked: it must come from this VM version's compiler. Never an error.
entries.example:
;; the bytecode of (lambda (x) x): GET_LOCAL 0, RETURN
(define code (cfasl-compress (list->string (map integer->char '(7 0 20)))))
(define id (cfasl-make-stub code 3 1 8 #f #f #()))
(cfasl-stub? id)     ; => #t
(cfasl-call id 42)   ; => 42

entries.name: cfasl-call
entries.desc: Decompress the bytecode of a procedure stub and run it with the arguments.
entries.returns: The value the procedure returns (void when called without a stub). Errors: a wrong argument count ("cfasl-call: expected N arguments, got M"; at least N - 1 for a variadic procedure), a corrupt stub ("cfasl_call_chunk: invalid chunk stub", "expected cfasl-stub object", "corrupt compressed data", "cfasl-call: corrupt stub", "empty procedure"), "procedure chunk exceeds scratch buffer limit (N > 32768)", "decompression failure", "out of memory". The bytecode itself is trusted (made by the compiler).
entries.example:
;; the bytecode of (lambda () 42): INT8 42, RETURN
(define code (cfasl-compress (list->string (map integer->char '(2 42 20)))))
(define answer (cfasl-make-stub code 3 0 8 #f #f #()))
(cfasl-call answer)            ; => 42
(cfasl-call (vector 1 2))      ; => error: invalid chunk stub

entries.name: cfasl-stub?
entries.desc: Whether obj is a procedure stub made by cfasl-make-stub.
entries.returns: #t for a stub (a vector of 8 or more elements whose first is the symbol cfasl-stub), else #f. Never an error.

entries.name: json-parse
entries.desc: JSON text to data: objects become alists with symbol keys, arrays vectors, null ().
entries.returns: The value of the JSON document (see the mapping). Errors: "json-parse: invalid JSON at byte N" (also for text after the value), "json-parse: nesting deeper than 32", text not a string.
entries.example:
(define doc (json-parse "{\"t\":\"temp\",\"v\":21.5,\"s\":[1,2],\"ok\":true,\"x\":null}"))
doc                      ; => ((t . "temp") (v . 21.5) (s . #(1 2)) (ok . #t) (x))
(cdr (assq 'v doc))      ; => 21.5
(json-parse "[1,")       ; => error: json-parse: invalid JSON at byte 3
entries.notes:
Mapping (json-parse, and json-stringify back):

| JSON | Scheme |
|---|---|
| object `{"a":1}` | association list with symbol keys `((a . 1))`, members in document order |
| array `[1,2]` | vector `#(1 2)` |
| string | string (UTF-8; escapes decoded, `\uXXXX` surrogate pairs combined) |
| integer `42`, `-7` | exact integer (bignum when large) |
| number with `.` or exponent | flonum |
| `true` / `false` | `#t` / `#f` |
| `null` | `()` |

An empty object `{}` also parses to `()`, so it is written back as `null`.
json-stringify also accepts string keys and writes symbols in value position as
strings. Read members with `assq`: `(cdr (assq 'temp obj))`.

entries.name: json-stringify
entries.desc: Data to compact JSON text (the inverse of json-parse).
entries.returns: A string without whitespace: alists (symbol or string keys) become objects, vectors arrays, strings and symbols JSON strings (", \ and control characters escaped, UTF-8 kept), exact integers and finite flonums numbers, #t/#f true/false, () null. Error "json-stringify: cannot encode X" for anything else (procedures, characters, improper lists, NaN or infinities).

entries.name: base64-encode
entries.desc: Base64 text of a string's bytes (standard alphabet, = padding, no line breaks).
entries.returns: A string of Base64 text (RFC 4648 alphabet with + and /, padded with =); "" for "". Error "base64-encode: expected a string".

entries.name: base64-decode
entries.desc: The bytes of Base64 text as a string; padding optional, whitespace ignored.
entries.returns: A string of the decoded bytes. The = padding may be left out; spaces and line breaks are skipped. Error "base64-decode: invalid Base64" for another character or a wrong length, and for a str that is not a string.

entries.name: url-encode
entries.desc: Percent-encode a string for a URL query: every byte but A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ . ~ becomes %XX.
entries.returns: A string: unreserved characters (RFC 3986: letters, digits, - _ . ~) kept, every other byte as %XX with uppercase hex (a space is %20, UTF-8 characters byte by byte). Error "url-encode: expected a string".

entries.name: url-decode
entries.desc: Decode percent-encoding (and + as space).
entries.returns: A string: each %XX (either case) becomes its byte and + a space; a % not followed by two hex digits is kept as is. Error "url-decode: expected a string".

entries.name: crc32
entries.desc: CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3, as zlib and PNG) of a string's bytes.
entries.returns: An exact integer 0..4294967295 (reflected polynomial #xEDB88320, initial value and final XOR #xFFFFFFFF). Error "crc32: expected a string".

entries.name: random
entries.desc: A pseudo-random integer in 0..n-1.
entries.returns: An exact integer 0 <= r < n. Seeded from the hardware random generator at boot (other sequences every start) unless random-seed! is called. Error "random: expected a positive integer" when n is not an integer >= 1.

entries.name: random-seed!
entries.desc: Seed the generator: the same seed gives the same numbers on every device and the simulator.
entries.returns: Void. n: any exact integer (only its low 32 bits count). Error "random-seed!: expected an integer".

entries.name: esp32-mac
entries.desc: The factory MAC address of the WiFi station as "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff".
entries.returns: A string of 17 characters: six lowercase hex byte pairs joined by colons, read from the eFuse (the same on every boot, a unique device id). Never an error.

entries.name: esp32-reset-reason
entries.desc: Why the chip last started: 'power-on, 'software, 'panic, 'watchdog, 'brownout, 'deep-sleep or 'other.
entries.returns: A symbol: power-on (power or the reset pin), software ((restart) or a firmware update), panic (a crash), watchdog (a task or interrupt watchdog), brownout (supply voltage dropped), deep-sleep (woke from (deep-sleep)), other. Never an error.

entries.name: esp32-idf-version
entries.desc: The ESP-IDF version the firmware was built with, e.g. "v6.1".
entries.returns: A string as the ESP-IDF reports it, e.g. "v6.1" (a development build may add a suffix such as "-dev-123-gabcdef"). Never an error.

entries.name: esp32-touch-read
entries.desc: Raw value of a capacitive touch pad (0..9); lower when touched.
entries.returns: A non-negative integer, the raw charge count of pad T0..T9 (GPIO 4, 0, 2, 15, 13, 12, 14, 27, 33, 32); it drops when a finger is near, so compare it with an untouched reading. The first read of a pad sets it up. Error "esp32-touch-read: pad must be 0..9".

entries.name: esp32-psram-size
entries.desc: Bytes of external PSRAM, 0 without.
entries.returns: A non-negative integer: the size of the external PSRAM in bytes (e.g. 4194304), 0 on a board without one. Never an error.

entries.name: fasl-to-c
entries.desc: Write a FASL file as an 8-byte aligned C array named name; with exe? #t also a main() that runs it.
entries.returns: #t when out was written; #f when in is empty or cannot be read in full. Errors: "%fasl-to-c: expected (fasl-path out-path sym-name is-exe)" (exe? must be a boolean), "cannot open 'in' for reading", "cannot create 'out'". The header declares name[] and name_len.

entries.name: file-remove
entries.desc: Delete a host file.
entries.returns: #t when deleted; #f when it does not exist, cannot be deleted or path is not a string. Never an error.

entries.name: file-size
entries.desc: Size of a host file in bytes, or -1.
entries.returns: An integer (bytes); -1 when the file cannot be opened or path is not a string. Never an error.

entries.name: system
entries.desc: Run a host shell command and wait for it.
entries.returns: The integer C system() returns: the exit code on Windows; on POSIX the wait status (exit code times 256). Error "system: expected command string".

entries.name: write-file-string
entries.desc: Create or replace a host file with the bytes of a string.
entries.returns: #t when all bytes were written; #f when the file cannot be created. Error "%write-file-string: expected (filepath string)" when an argument is not a string.
